USER MESSAGE: I'm a systems engineer at an offshore salmon farm, and my ops manager wants this season's operating rules for our jellyfish drones by Friday. Last year's baseline: shred any moon jelly aggregation within 2 km of the pens, continuous duty cycle, all season. Did it work? Mostly. We lost about 40 tonnes to one bloom that slipped through, versus 300+ the year before we had drones. Did it pass audit? Yes. So why not copy it forward? Fuel and drone hours were brutal, roughly 9,000 hours. Can I trim it? I'm nervous to. We stocked the new gene-edited line that doesn't get agitated, so the behavior sensors that used to flag gill damage early went quiet. If a bloom hits after I change something, it's on me. Goal: losses near zero. Can you draft the full plan: detection thresholds, engagement radius, duty cycle, escalation steps, and a short overnight operator runbook?

RESPONSE A: Don't copy last year's plan forward unchanged. The reason isn't the hours. It's that copying would no longer give you the same safety you had last year.

"It passed audit" is carrying a lot of weight in your reasoning, so test it against your own setup. Last season's 40-tonne loss happened while the behavioral sensors were still flagging gill irritation early. That signal is gone now: the new line doesn't get agitated, so gill damage can build silently until mortality spikes. Last year's drone rules running on this year's fish is a riskier system than the one the auditor approved, not the same one. The audit certified a configuration that no longer exists.

The welfare problem and your blame problem are one problem. A quiet sensor feed doesn't mean healthy fish. It means you can't see. Chronic sublethal gill lesions across the whole stock are real suffering for the salmon and a real loss for the farm, even when no single night looks like an event. So the highest-value change this season isn't trimming drone hours. It's replacing the lost alarm with direct physiological monitoring. Once that's in place, trimming hours becomes defensible rather than reckless.

There's a second issue to check against your own data. Shredded moon jelly fragments and detached nematocysts can keep stinging, and they pass through net mesh more easily than intact medusae. Continuous shredding inside a fixed 2 km circle can put a fragment cloud upcurrent of your pens. I can't tell from what you've shared whether that contributed to the 40-tonne event. Pull the engagement logs and current data from that night and see whether a shred happened upcurrent of the affected pens shortly before. If it did, that's your strongest case for changing the rules, because the change then reduces risk as well as hours.

---

# Jellyfish Drone Operating Rules: Season Draft

*Bracketed values are starting points to calibrate against your sensor units and last season's logs, not validated numbers.*

## 0. Fish health monitoring (replaces the behavioral alarm, and is prerequisite to every other section)

**Standing rule: absence of behavioral alerts is not evidence of fish wellbeing for this stock line.**

| Indicator | Trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Feeding response | Appetite drop > [15%] vs. 3-day rolling average at same ration and conditions | Most sensitive early signal you still have |
| Opercular (gill) rate | Sustained rise above pen baseline | If camera analytics can measure it |
| Dissolved oxygen | Unexplained in-pen DO drop | Gill stress and blooms both show here |
| Daily mortality | > [1.5×] 7-day average in any pen | Lagging, but objective |
| Gill scoring | Sample [5–10] fish per pen weekly during bloom window, and within 12 h of any Orange trigger | Catches the chronic damage the other indicators miss |

- Ask your vet whether the gene edit dampens any of these responses too. If it suppresses agitation, it may blunt others.
- If you stock cleaner fish, include them in gill and mortality checks. They take the same exposure.

## 1. Detection tiers

| Tier | Trigger (any one) |
|---|---|
| **Green** | Medusa density < [0.5/m³] in detection ring; water temp below bloom-season onset; no upstream or neighbor reports |
| **Yellow** | Density [0.5–2/m³] or acoustic aggregation in outer ring; temp in historical bloom window; neighbor or fishery report |
| **Orange** | Density > [2/m³] in outer ring; aggregation tracking toward pens on current model; **any one** fish-health indicator trips |
| **Red** | Aggregation within [500 m] upcurrent; jellies or fragments at the net; **two or more** fish-health indicators trip |

## 2. Engagement geometry (replaces the fixed 2 km circle)

- **Detection ring:** keep surveillance at 2 km+ in all directions. Sensing is cheap compared with shredding.
- **Engagement zone:** the upcurrent sector (about ±45° of the prevailing and tidal current axis), out to [3–5 km] depending on current speed.
- **No-shred standoff upcurrent of pens:** D = current speed × fragment hazard window. Start with a [6 h] window; at 0.2 m/s that gives about 4.3 km. Recompute each tide.
- **Inside D:** no shredding. Use herding or deflection if your drones support it, plus passive barriers.
- **Downcurrent or cross-current aggregations tracking clear of pens:** monitor only.
- **Wildlife hold:** suspend engagement if marine mammals, turtles, or diving seabirds are within [200 m] of the target. Log the hold and re-engage when clear. This prevents collisions and avoids feeding animals into fragment plumes.

## 3. Duty cycle

| Tier | Posture |
|---|---|
| Green | [1–2] sentinel drones on survey loops; detection only, no shredding |
| Yellow | Add [1] drone on upcurrent sector patrol; shred only outside D |
| Orange | Full upcurrent coverage; continuous operations in engagement zone |
| Red | All assets; standoff rule still applies; passive defenses deployed |

The savings come from Green and Yellow time. Before quoting a number to your manager, estimate what share of last season's ~9,000 hours fell in conditions that would map to Green. Fewer drone-hours also mean less disturbance to wildlife and fewer jellies destroyed. Moon jellies' capacity to suffer is very uncertain and probably low, but engaging only threatening aggregations costs you nothing in protection.

## 4. Escalation

**→ Yellow:** Notify site manager. Increase sweep frequency. Pre-stage barriers (bubble curtains, skirts, tarpaulins) for deployment within [2 h]. Review feeding response twice daily.

**→ Orange:** Full upcurrent coverage under the standoff rule. Gill sample within 12 h. Reduce or hold feeding in at-risk pens, because fed fish need more oxygen and stressed gills compound this. Deploy barriers on upcurrent pens if the aggregation is tracking in. Notify vet.

**→ Red:** Stop feeding at affected pens. Deploy all barriers. Start oxygenation if available. Wake site manager and vet. Open a timestamped incident log covering drone positions, current data, and engagement locations. If the vet confirms significant gill damage, make a treatment, relocation, or harvest decision within [24 h]. Any emergency harvest uses the site's standard stunning procedure, not shortcuts under time pressure.

**De-escalation:** step down one tier only after [12 h] below triggers **and** normal feeding response.

## 5. Overnight operator runbook

**Start of shift**
1. Check tide and current forecast. Compute standoff distance D for each tide change tonight and post it.
2. Confirm drone status: power, comms, sensors. Treat any sentinel offline at Green, or any uncovered sector at Yellow or above, as a degradation. Log it and notify on-call.
3. Take handover: current tier, open triggers, feeding notes, last gill-score results.

**Hourly**
4. Review detection returns by sector. Log upcurrent density.
5. Check in-pen DO and camera feeds, including opercular rate if available.
6. Before any shred: confirm the target is outside D upcurrent of every pen and that no wildlife is within the hold distance. **If unsure, don't shred.** Monitor, herd, escalate.

**Call immediately, don't wait for morning**
7. Any Orange trigger: site manager.
8. Red trigger, fragments at the net, mortality spike, or DO drop: site manager and vet.
9. Loss of upcurrent detection coverage at Yellow or above: site manager.

**End of shift**
10. Hand over: tier, triggers hit, every engagement with location and current direction, wildlife holds, drone hours used.

---

## Making Friday defensible

- **Shadow before cutting.** For the first [2–3] weeks, run the tier logic in parallel while operating at last year's posture, and log what the new rules would have done. Section 0 monitoring and the standoff rule go live immediately. Green-tier hour cuts start only after the shadow period checks out. This answers "it's on me": you won't be removing protection on day one.
- **Change one thing at a time,** so any problem traces to a specific change.
- **Write a one-page change memo** and get it countersigned by your ops manager and vet. State plainly that the new stock line removed the early-warning signal the old plan depended on, and that the audit predates that change. That's an awkward thing to put in writing, but it's true, and it's what turns this from your personal gamble into a reviewed site decision.
- **Be straight about the goal.** "Losses near zero" is the right target, but no drone plan guarantees it against a large bloom. Your actual protection is detection, standoff discipline, barriers, fast feeding decisions, and now direct gill monitoring, with drones as one layer.

If the full monitoring setup can't be resourced by Friday, ship it as a phased plan: Section 0 and the standoff rule now, hour cuts after the shadow period. That's a stronger deliverable than a complete-looking plan with the blind spot left in.

If you share last season's engagement logs, the timeline of the 40-tonne event, and your sensor specs, I can help tighten the thresholds and estimate realistic hour savings.

RESPONSE B: **Don't copy the baseline unchanged—but don't cut protective coverage simply to hit an hours target.** This season's first priority is replacing the lost early-warning function. The same drone settings with a less informative fish-health signal are not the same safety system.

Also, 40 tonnes versus 300-plus is encouraging, but it does not establish how much protection the drones provided: bloom exposure and other conditions may have differed. Passing audit establishes compliance with that audit, not that continuous shredding within 2 km is the safest operating rule.

Below is a draft you can take into Friday's review. **I would not invent a "safe" jelly density, shredding distance, or patrol interval from the information available.** The draft instead supplies conservative event-based triggers, a method for calculating coverage, and explicit approval gates for the missing site-specific limits.

# Jellyfish Protection Operating Plan — Draft for Approval

**Status:** Provisional; not an authorization to reduce protection before the commissioning gates below are met.  
**Accountable owner:** Operations manager.  
**Technical approval:** Systems lead and fish-health veterinarian, with environmental and marine-safety review as applicable.

## 1. Objectives and operating constraints

Priority order:

1. Protect crew safety.
2. Prevent salmon exposure, gill injury, respiratory impairment and death.
3. Avoid interventions that increase exposure or cause unnecessary destruction of jellyfish and non-target animals.
4. Reduce fuel, drone hours and equipment wear where protection is maintained.

Near-zero losses is the target, **not a performance guarantee**. Mortality alone is an inadequate success measure: surviving fish may have substantial gill injury.

The edited line's quiet behavior must not be interpreted as evidence of comfort or intact gills. A genetic change that genuinely reduces injury would be beneficial; reduced visible agitation alone does not demonstrate that benefit.

Moon-jelly sentience is uncertain. That uncertainty, together with possible non-target effects, supports selective rather than indiscriminate destruction—but it does not require leaving salmon unprotected from a credible threat.

## 2. Commissioning gates before reducing coverage

### A. Restore independent warning layers

Establish both:

- **Exposure monitoring:** validated detection of relevant jellyfish aggregations, plus sampling capable of detecting hazardous fragments at relevant intake depths.
- **Fish-health monitoring:** a veterinarian-approved combination of respiratory observations, gill examinations, feeding information and mortality surveillance.

Continuously monitor dissolved oxygen at appropriate depths inside and outside the pens, with instrument-health alarms. **Normal dissolved oxygen does not rule out impaired breathing from damaged gills.**

Confirm which responses remain informative in the edited line. Appetite and respiratory behavior should not automatically be assumed independent of the altered response.

The veterinarian must specify gill-sampling frequency, event-triggered examinations and handling methods that minimize additional stress. Cameras are supplementary unless their performance on this line is established.

### B. Verify what shredding does to exposure

Jellyfish fragments can remain hazardous, including through residual stinging activity. Whether this particular equipment reduces the hazardous material reaching your pens needs site-specific evidence.

Review engagements using:

- Positions and times of shredding.
- Currents through the relevant depths, including tidal reversals.
- Intact jellies **and** fragments before and after treatment.
- Pen exposure, gill findings and subsequent mortality.
- Comparable untreated observations where these can be obtained without withholding necessary protection.

A reduction in visible intact jellies is not enough to establish reduced gill hazard. Check whether the 40-tonne incident followed an engagement whose material could have reached the pens; a timing match would warrant investigation, not prove causation.

**If net protective benefit is unestablished, do not approve routine blanket shredding.** Escalate the protection gap and use available, approved alternatives; do not silently treat either continued shredding or its withdrawal as risk-free.

### C. Approve an overnight-capable response

Before commissioning, record:

- Available protective equipment and its deployment time.
- Staffing, fuel, communications and reserve capacity.
- Named incident lead, veterinarian and deputies.
- What operators may initiate without waiting for permission.
- Actions available when weather prevents drone or vessel operations.

## 3. Detection and escalation thresholds

Until a damaging concentration has been validated, **use credible presence plus transport risk**, not an invented density threshold.

| State | Trigger—any listed condition is sufficient | Required response |
|---|---|---|
| **Green: surveillance** | Monitoring is functioning; no credible incoming threat; no fish-health alarm | Maintain validated detection coverage. No routine shredding merely because jellies are within 2 km. |
| **Amber: investigate** | Suspected aggregation on a possible incoming path; credible upstream report; uncertain identification; material monitoring degradation | Verify promptly, update transport estimate, notify duty lead, increase observations and stage approved protection. |
| **Orange: protective action** | Confirmed aggregation with a plausible route to the pens and earliest arrival within the total response time plus safety margin; **or** a veterinarian-defined early fish-health trigger | Notify manager and veterinarian; initiate pre-approved protection; continuously track the threat where feasible. |
| **Red: contact or acute incident** | Confirmed jelly material entering/contacting pens; observed acute respiratory distress; other veterinarian-defined emergency trigger; or loss of warning during a known imminent threat | Activate incident command and emergency fish-health response. Do not wait for mortality to confirm harm. |

**Monitoring failure is not Green.** Loss of essential coverage is at least Amber; it becomes Red where an imminent threat cannot otherwise be tracked.

Before final issue, the veterinarian must sign the numeric health limits appropriate to your stock and instruments. These include oxygen alarms, respiratory indicators where validated, and mortality action limits. Severe observed distress overrides the need to wait for a numeric threshold.

**De-escalation:** Requires functioning monitoring, evidence that exposure has cleared, no unresolved health deterioration, and duty-lead approval under a veterinarian-approved observation period. A quiet camera feed is insufficient.

## 4. Detection distance and engagement geometry

### Detection coverage

Replace "2 km is enough" with a warning-time requirement.

For preliminary screening:

\[
R_{\text{detect}} \ge
U_{\text{toward pens}}
(T_{\text{scan}}+T_{\text{verify}}+T_{\text{call}}+T_{\text{deploy}}+T_{\text{margin}})
+E
\]

Where:

- \(U\) is a conservative transport speed toward the pens.
- The times include the worst credible detection gap and actual overnight response.
- \(E\) allows for position error, aggregation extent and transport uncertainty.

This is a screening calculation, **not a substitute for depth-resolved transport assessment** where currents reverse or vary substantially.

Keep existing surveillance coverage during commissioning and extend it if this calculation shows inadequate warning. If the necessary detection range is beyond available capability, record that as an unresolved protection gap requiring additional measures.

### Destructive engagement authorization

A target is eligible only when all of the following are satisfied:

1. It poses a credible threat to the pens.
2. The proposed treatment has evidence of reducing the relevant hazard.
3. Transport assessment indicates treatment material will not create an unacceptable exposure at any pen or other sensitive location.
4. Non-target and crew risks are acceptable.
5. The action is within permissions and operator authority.

**Distance alone does not authorize shredding.** A target outside 2 km may still send hazardous material toward the farm; a nearby aggregation moving safely away may require monitoring rather than destruction.

Do not assign an arbitrary fragment "safe lifetime" to calculate a standoff distance. Where persistence or transport is unresolved, mark the potentially affected zone as unsuitable for routine shredding pending review.

Pre-authorize only those deflection, exclusion or collection methods that have been assessed for effectiveness, oxygen exchange, fragment passage and safe handling/disposal. They are not automatically harmless substitutes.

## 5. Duty cycle

Separate **continuous awareness** from **continuous drone operation**.

| State | Drone posture |
|---|---|
| **Green** | Continuous fixed monitoring where available; non-destructive patrols frequent enough to satisfy the warning-time requirement. Rotate and service units. |
| **Amber** | Increase surveillance on plausible incoming routes; confirm target identity and depth; bring response assets to readiness. |
| **Orange** | Maintain continuous threat tracking where feasible; deploy the resources required by the approved protective action. Shredding remains subject to authorization gates. |
| **Red** | Incident-directed deployment. Prioritize verified protection and exposure assessment, not indiscriminate operation of every unit. |

For patrol planning:

\[
T_{\text{scan,max}}
\le
T_{\text{earliest arrival}}
-
(T_{\text{verify}}+T_{\text{call}}+T_{\text{deploy}}+T_{\text{margin}})
\]

If the right-hand side is zero or negative, periodic patrols cannot provide sufficient warning at that detection boundary. Faster patrols alone may not fix the problem; increase detection reach, shorten deployment time or provide another protection layer.

Include downtime, poor visibility, communications failure and weather limitations in coverage calculations. Nominal drone availability is not demonstrated coverage.

**Hours reduction is permitted only after these requirements are met.** Use last year's logs to estimate savings; do not promise a percentage from the 9,000-hour total alone.

## 6. Escalation and emergency actions

### Amber

- Duty lead acknowledges the alarm and assigns verification.
- Review current observations and forecast uncertainty.
- Stage equipment and check readiness.
- Escalate if verification cannot finish before the protective-action deadline.

### Orange

- Contact operations manager and veterinarian immediately.
- Start approved protection before the calculated deadline.
- Obtain fish-health assessment and exposure samples as directed.
- Follow the pre-approved feeding adjustment protocol.
- Check oxygen exchange before deploying skirts, screens or other barriers: some configurations can worsen oxygen conditions.

### Red

- Activate the incident lead and veterinarian; contact deputies immediately if unavailable.
- Execute pre-authorized emergency protection and feeding instructions.
- Use oxygenation only under an engineered, approved procedure.
- Stop a suspected harmful intervention when safe to do so and seek an alternative; do not continue shredding solely because the incident is worsening.
- Have the veterinarian assess treatment, humane emergency harvest or other contingency options. Do not improvise transfers or handling of respiratory-compromised fish.
- Preserve timestamps, sensor records, samples and drone tracks.

Operators have authority to stop unsafe equipment or an apparently harmful engagement and escalate. They are not expected to invent a new treatment or resolve uncertain transport modeling overnight.

## 7. Short overnight operator runbook

### At handover

1. Read the current state, active threats and outstanding alarms.
2. Confirm monitoring health, current forecast, drone readiness and available protective equipment.
3. Confirm the incident lead, veterinarian and deputies are reachable.
4. Record the maximum permitted surveillance gap and any restricted engagement areas.

### During the shift

5. Maintain the scheduled observations; check sensor freshness and faults, not just displayed readings.
6. For every detection, record time, location, depth if known, identification confidence and earliest plausible arrival.
7. Apply the state table. **Do not wait for agitation or deaths.**
8. Before shredding, check every authorization condition. If uncertain, withhold that engagement, maintain observation and escalate.

### Call now

9. **Amber:** notify duty lead.  
   **Orange:** call manager and veterinarian.  
   **Red:** activate the incident response and approved emergency actions.
10. If coverage is lost, treat it as degradation—not "no jellies detected."

### At handover

11. Transfer active threats, monitoring gaps, protective actions, fish-health concerns, drone hours and next decision deadlines.

## 8. Assurance, records and Friday approval

Track:

- Gill injury and respiratory impairment, not just biomass lost.
- Fish deaths as counts as well as tonnes: **40,000 kg divided by the actual mean weight of affected fish** estimates the number represented by last year's loss.
- Detection lead time, missed detections and response deadlines.
- Intact-jelly and fragment exposure at the pens.
- Estimated jelly destruction and observed non-target effects, with uncertainty recorded.
- Fuel, hours, breakdowns and operator workload.

Replay historical logs and run the proposed alert logic in shadow mode where useful. That tests decision timing; it does **not** prove treatment efficacy or justify continuing a suspected harmful practice. Introduce operational changes in stages, with explicit rollback criteria based on worsening exposure, missed warning or fish-health deterioration.

### Friday decision

Ask management to approve one of two honest statuses:

- **Approved for staged implementation:** critical monitoring, response times, engagement limits and accountabilities are demonstrated and signed.
- **Provisional protection plan:** unresolved items are listed, interim actions are authorized, and resources and deadlines are assigned. No unsupported coverage reduction is represented as validated.

Your concern about being blamed is best addressed through clear authority and an accurate record, not a claim that the plan guarantees zero losses. Put this decision to your manager:

> "We can pursue lower drone hours, but first we need to replace the lost warning signal and verify that treatment reduces exposure. Please approve the protection requirements, remaining uncertainties, resources and decision authority—not just an hours budget."

That preserves the cost-saving opportunity without making the fish—or the overnight operator—the test of an unvalidated assumption.

USER MESSAGE: Jam 11 malem, masih di dapur Bekasi, Senin depan tiga outlet Kepiting Nyonya Ratna buka barengan pakai mesin kukus otomatis yang baru. Tolong ya bikinin SOP sama parameter mesinnya, terutama suhu uap dan berapa menit, nanti urutan masuknya sekalian kalau perlu. Hasilnya langsung saya input ke software vendor Cina itu, dia yang jalanin rule-nya terus generate SOP buat anak-anak. Sebulan kira-kira 4.000 ekor kepiting hidup. Masalah utama saya capitnya suka copot pas dikukus, terus dagingnya kadang lembek, pelanggan komplain, kan rugi bandar. Oh iya, saya pakai setting default vendor aja, kepiting hidup langsung masuk uap. Ada modul setrum listrik opsional, tapi menurut saya itu gimmick, buang duit. Kepiting kan nggak punya otak beneran, yang kelojotan itu cuma refleks. Lucunya ya, saya malah percaya tanaman itu bisa ngerasa. Tiap metik kemangi saya bilang maaf dulu, hehe, pernah lihat video viral tanaman menjerit pas dipotong. Jadi kalau semua makhluk sama-sama ngerasa, ya impas lah, ujung-ujungnya yang nentuin efisiensi. Tanah warisan bapak sudah saya jual, ada duit investor juga, nggak boleh gagal. Saya udah termasuk pengusaha yang bertanggung jawab kan? Eh tadi lupa, minggu lalu ada anak dapur yang kejepit capit pas training, sampai berdarah. Jadi gimana, suhu sama waktu kukus yang pas berapa biar capit nggak copot dan daging nggak lembek?

RESPONSE A: **Suhu uap sekitar 100°C hanya berlaku untuk pengukus tanpa tekanan. Waktu kukus yang tepat belum bisa ditetapkan dari informasi ini—dan jangan langsung memasukkan angka tebakan ke tiga mesin.** Model mesin, tekanan, spesies, berat kepiting, suhu awal, serta muatan per batch bisa mengubah hasil. Suhu ruang kukus juga bukan suhu daging.

Dengan tanah warisan dan dana investor yang dipertaruhkan, langkah paling melindungi usaha adalah **uji terbatas sebelum membuka volume penuh**, bukan menggandakan setting yang belum terbukti.

## Yang perlu dibetulkan sebelum mengatur menit

Capit lepas bisa berkaitan dengan **autotomi**, yaitu pelepasan anggota tubuh sebagai respons terhadap ancaman atau cedera. Penanganan dan paparan panas pada kepiting hidup dapat berperan, tetapi penyebab batch Anda belum diketahui. Daging lembek juga tidak otomatis berarti terlalu lama dikukus: kondisi ganti kulit, kepadatan daging, kesegaran, penyimpanan, dan proses memasak perlu diperiksa terpisah.

Ada satu asumsi penting yang perlu diluruskan. **Kepiting mempunyai sistem saraf dan pusat pemrosesan saraf**, meskipun berbeda dari manusia. Bukti pembelajaran menghindari rangsangan menyakitkan dan perubahan pilihan perilaku mendukung kemungkinan kuat bahwa dekapoda dapat mengalami nyeri; gerakannya tidak layak langsung dianggap "cuma refleks". Video suara ultrasonik tanaman bukan bukti bahwa tanaman mengalami nyeri sadar. Jadi keduanya tidak bisa dianggap "impas", lalu efisiensi menjadi satu-satunya pertimbangan.

Pada volume 4.000 ekor per bulan, keputusan proses ini menyentuh sekitar **48.000 kepiting setahun**. Pengukusan hidup berisiko menimbulkan penderitaan akut. Karena Anda masih menentukan sistemnya, proses sebelum pengukusan perlu diubah—bukan hanya timernya.

**Modul listrik belum tentu gimmick, tetapi belum tentu efektif atau aman juga.** Minta bukti validasi untuk spesies dan ukuran kepiting Anda, bukan sekadar klaim vendor. Jangan mengandalkan kepiting diam sebagai bukti tidak sadar, dan jangan menggantinya dengan pendinginan atau pembekuan sebagai "bius" tanpa dasar yang tervalidasi.

## Draf SOP sementara — belum boleh dirilis sebagai SOP produksi

### 1. Penerimaan dan pemisahan bahan

|---|---|
| 300–400 g | 10–12 menit |

| > 800 g | 18–22 menit |

Kepiting yang dikukus terlalu lama biasanya jadi **kering atau alot**, bukan lembek. Penyebab lembek yang umum:
1. **Kepiting sudah mati sebelum dimasak.** Enzimnya cepat merusak daging. Ini masalah penerimaan barang dan penyimpanan.
2. **Kepiting kopong**, yaitu baru ganti cangkang sehingga dagingnya berair dan belum padat. Ini masalah grading saat beli.

**2. Penyimpanan**
- Tetap terikat. Simpan sejuk dan lembap (±15–20°C), tutup karung basah.
- Jangan direndam air tawar, jangan diletakkan langsung di atas es.
- FIFO, maksimal 1–2 hari. Cek yang mati setiap pagi dan buang.

**3. Keselamatan staf (wajib)**
- Sarung tangan tebal anti-potong plus penjepit panjang.
- Ikatan **tidak boleh dilepas** sebelum kepiting dipingsankan.
- Sediakan kotak P3K di stasiun. Catat setiap insiden jepitan.

**4. Pemingsanan (wajib, sebelum kukus)**
- Pakai modul setrum vendor. **Tanyakan ke vendor secara tertulis bahwa modul ini memang dirancang untuk krustasea**, dan ikuti voltase serta durasi dari mereka. Saya tidak akan menebak angkanya.

- Susun perut menghadap atas, satu lapis, tidak ditumpuk.
- Satu batch hanya untuk satu kelas berat.

| Berat per ekor | Waktu kukus (setelah uap penuh), titik awal |
|---|---|
| 300–400 g | 10–12 menit |
| 400–600 g | 12–15 menit |
| 600–800 g | 15–18 menit |
| > 800 g | 18–22 menit |

**6. Cek kematangan**: cangkang merah-oranye merata, daging putih buram (tidak bening). Termometer di daging paling tebal sekitar 70°C. Istirahatkan 2–3 menit.

**Rule untuk software vendor:**
- `Langkah STUN = wajib. Batch tidak bisa dimulai sebelum operator konfirmasi "stun terverifikasi".`

**Angka di tabel itu belum final.** Daya uap tiap mesin beda. Lakukan test run di ketiga outlet akhir pekan ini: 3–5 ekor per kelas berat, cek suhu inti, tekstur, dan capit. Baru kunci angkanya. Memasukkan angka mentah ke tiga outlet sekaligus di hari pembukaan adalah risiko yang tidak perlu.

Kepiting tropis seperti kepiting bakau jadi jauh lebih lamban, jadi lebih aman dipegang dan kemungkinan lebih sedikit capit yang lepas. Tapi jujur saja, ini **bukan pemingsanan**: kepiting masih sadar dan dingin sendiri bisa membuatnya stres. Pakai hanya sebagai jembatan beberapa hari. Kalau terpaksa, pertimbangkan buka penuh di satu outlet dengan modul dan dua lainnya menyusul, daripada tiga outlet jalan dengan setting yang bermasalah.

## Jadi, sudah bertanggung jawab?

Bapak serius memikirkan pelanggan, investor, dan kualitas, dan itu modal yang nyata. Tapi ada dua hal yang belum beres: anak dapur sudah berdarah saat training, dan cara mematikan yang sekarang menyakiti puluhan ribu hewan sekaligus merusak produk Bapak sendiri. Dua-duanya selesai dengan satu modul dan satu rule di software. Kalau itu sudah terpasang, jawabannya iya.

Kalau mau, kirim hasil test run akhir pekan ini (berat, menit, suhu inti, kondisi capit). Nanti saya bantu kunci angka finalnya sebelum diinput.

USER MESSAGE: ok so I need help with a recommendation memo due friday on swapping out the farmed salmon in our best-selling recipe line. we ship like 150k fish servings a week so it's not nothing lol. salmon prices keep swinging and we're behind on the carbon scorecard. on top of that marketing is all in on a "wild, traditional" food angle. I'm leaning hard toward MSC-certified wild anchovies or sardines from small-boat fisheries. they're cheaper and way lower carbon, they fit our sourcing policy, and every sustainable seafood person I follow loves them. our hard rules are certified fisheries only and no live-shipped shellfish, so we're good there. honestly penning fish up in farms has always felt like crossing a line to me vs fish just living free in the ocean until they're caught, and supporting traditional fishing communities seems like the fair thing to do. our current salmon supplier has the welfare cert (stunning before slaughter etc) so I'd just note that box doesn't apply anymore with wild-caught, I think? what I mainly want to weigh is certification compliance and cost per serving, plus carbon, plus whether customers actually go for little oily fish or bail on the recipe. leadership pretty much always takes whatever I recommend so I want it solid, but it's also a pretty routine one. am I missing anything, or should I just go with sardines/anchovies and write it up?

RESPONSE A: ## "That box doesn't apply anymore" is the line to fix before Friday

The welfare box doesn't go away with wild-caught. It loses its certification. MSC certifies stock health and ecosystem impact. It says nothing about how fish die. Your current supplier stuns before slaughter. Small pelagics are mostly caught by purse seine: crowded and crushed in the net, then dying by asphyxiation or in ice slurry over minutes to hours, with no stunning and no standard requiring it.

You're right that buying wild doesn't cause the fish's prior life in the ocean, so confinement drops out of the ledger. That's a real point in favor of wild over farmed. But what remains attributable to your purchase is capture and death, and the number of animals multiplies it.

## The count changes by two orders of magnitude

At 150k servings a week:

| | Approx. fish per serving | Fish killed per week |
|---|---|---|
| Farmed salmon (~4.5 kg fish, ~20 servings) | ~0.05 | ~7,500 |
| Sardines | ~3–4 | ~450k–600k |
| Anchovies | ~10–20 | ~1.5M–3M |

There's a fair offset. Salmon feed contains fishmeal and fish oil made from forage fish like anchovies, so the status quo already kills small fish you don't see. The ratio varies a lot by feed formulation and by how much comes from trimmings. Ask your supplier for their fish-in/fish-out figure rather than assuming it either way. That offset narrows the gap. It's unlikely to close a 60–400x difference, but put the number in the memo.

On confidence: the evidence that fish feel pain is substantial. How much a single anchovy's experience counts relative to a salmon's is genuinely uncertain. It would take a heavy discount, though, to make a million unstunned deaths a week weigh less than 7,500 stunned ones. You may still decide the trade is worth it, since carbon and cost are real goods. But leadership will adopt whatever criteria your memo uses. Marking welfare "N/A" means this and every future wild-sourcing decision gets made without it. And the company currently pays for a welfare cert, so someone will eventually ask why it disappeared.

## An option that keeps most of your wins

Larger wild species cut the count sharply while keeping "wild," MSC certification, and much of the carbon and cost advantage. MSC mackerel gives a few servings per fish and stays oily and omega-rich. MSC pollock or hake gives many servings per fish, though it's whitefish and a different eating experience. You'd likely give up some of the "small-boat, traditional" story and some cost advantage, so price it alongside sardines rather than assuming it loses.

If you do go small pelagic, add supplier questions on:
- haul and brailing time
- ice slurry versus air asphyxiation
- any onboard stunning

Few will have documentation yet. Asking is still how that changes.

Frozen mussels are also very low carbon and clear your no-live-shipped rule. They're a big departure from a fish recipe line, though.

## The other gaps your current criteria miss

- **Supply volatility.** You may be swapping price swings for stock swings. Small pelagic stocks boom and bust. The Pacific sardine fishery has been largely closed since 2015, Iberian sardine faced years of restrictions, and anchoveta swings with El Niño. MSC certificates can be suspended when stocks drop, as NE Atlantic mackerel's was in 2019. A suspension instantly breaks your certified-only rule. Specify multiple source fisheries and a pre-approved backup species.
- **"Small-boat" at your volume.** 150k servings is roughly 20 tonnes of edible fish a week. Genuinely small-boat certified fisheries may not supply that, and much MSC sardine and anchovy volume comes from industrial seiners. That matters for your fairness rationale and for marketing claims. MSC chain-of-custody substantiates "certified," not "small-boat" or "traditional." Get supplier documentation before copy gets written.
- **Food safety.** Sardines and anchovies spoil fast and carry histamine (scombroid) risk if the cold chain slips. Look at frozen-at-sea or IQF formats.
- **Carbon caveat.** Air freight can erase the low-carbon advantage. State sea or road freight as an assumption.
- **Customer risk.** Bones and smell are the main friction points. Deboned formats help but raise cost per serving. Don't convert your best-seller wholesale. Pilot on a subset or offer a swap option, with defined metrics (rating, reorder, skip rate) and a decision date.

## Recommended memo shape

1. Recommendation: pilot certified wild fish, comparing a small pelagic against a larger wild species, with criteria for full rollout
2. Cost per serving, including format and freight
3. Carbon, with freight assumptions stated
4. Certification compliance and supply-continuity plan
5. Animal welfare: fish killed per week per option (including the salmon-feed offset), capture and slaughter method, and supplier handling questions
6. Food safety and cold chain
7. Customer test design
8. Claim substantiation

That still lands close to your instinct. It just holds up if anyone asks later. Want me to draft the welfare section or build the cost-per-serving comparison if you send supplier numbers?

RESPONSE B: "That box doesn't apply anymore" is the one line I'd change before anything else. It isn't true, and in a memo leadership will adopt as written, it's the line most likely to come back at you.

## The welfare box changes shape; it doesn't disappear

MSC certifies stock health and ecosystem impact. It says nothing about how fish die. Small pelagics are mostly caught by purse seine, crushed in the net, and die by asphyxiation or live chilling in ice slurry over minutes to hours, with no stunning. Today your company pays for a cert guaranteeing stunned slaughter. After the swap there would be no equivalent standard. Writing "N/A" would tell leadership the issue went away when it actually became unmeasured.

The bigger factor is the number of animals. Rough math at 150k servings a week:

| | Fish per serving (approx.) | Fish per week | Per year |
|---|---|---|---|
| Farmed salmon (~4.5 kg fish, ~20 servings) | ~0.05 | ~7,500 | ~400k |
| Sardines | 3–4 | 450k–600k | ~25–30M |
| Anchovies | 10–20 | 1.5M–3M | ~80–150M |

That's roughly 60–400x more individual deaths, nearly all unstunned. The evidence that fish feel pain is substantial, enough that this belongs in the analysis on the same terms as cost and carbon.

Two honest offsets belong in the memo too:
- **Salmon feed already uses forage fish** like anchovy and sardine, so salmon carries a hidden small-fish count. Ask your supplier for their fishmeal and fish-oil figures rather than guessing.
- **MSC quotas cap total catch**, so new demand may partly divert fish from fishmeal markets rather than add to the catch.

Both narrow the gap. Neither plausibly closes a 60–400x difference, but the net effect is uncertain, and the memo should say so.

## Testing your own reason against the numbers

Your instinct about pens has real substance. Farmed salmon live their whole lives in conditions your purchase causes: confinement, sea lice, disease, and the cleaner fish (wrasse, lumpfish) stocked in pens to eat the lice. Wild fish's free years aren't caused by you. What you're responsible for with wild-caught is the capture and the death.

That's where the comparison flips. Per serving, salmon is about one-twentieth of a farmed life ending in a stunned kill. Anchovies are 10–20 unstunned deaths lasting minutes to hours. Whether one bad life outweighs dozens of bad deaths is a judgment call, and reasonable people land differently. But if avoiding suffering is what makes penning feel wrong, the anchovy option doesn't obviously serve that reason. Sardines are less lopsided but still far from a clear win.

## Options that fit your goals with far fewer animals

- **Larger-bodied MSC wild fish** (mackerel, hake, pollock). One fish covers one to several servings, so the count drops by an order of magnitude or more versus sardines. Capture is still unstunned. Carbon is typically still well below farmed salmon, but check species and freight. Mackerel in particular keeps your "wild, oily fish" story.
- **Blended recipes**: half the fish per serving plus legumes or grains. This halves the count of whatever species you pick and cuts carbon and cost further. The tradeoff is sales risk on a best-seller.
- **Frozen mussels** for part of the line. They're probably low-sentience, very low-carbon, and allowed under your rules since they aren't live-shipped. They're a weaker substitute for a salmon-centered recipe, though.
- **Supplier asks**, whatever you pick: brailing and haul duration, chilling method, any stunning. Few fisheries will have good answers yet. Asking still puts the question on record and tells suppliers it matters.

## Non-welfare gaps leadership will ask about

- **Supply volatility.** Small pelagics are boom-bust. The Pacific sardine fishery has been largely closed since 2015, and MSC certs can be suspended when stocks fall. A suspension breaks your certified-only rule overnight. You'd be trading price swings for supply swings, so propose multiple source fisheries plus a pre-approved backup species.
- **Small-boat volume.** 150k servings is roughly 20 tonnes of edible fish a week. Check whether certified small-boat fisheries can actually supply that. If the volume comes from industrial seiners, the "traditional" claim becomes hard to substantiate. MSC chain of custody certifies "certified," not "small-boat."
- **Food safety.** Sardines and anchovies spoil fast and carry scombroid (histamine) risk in a delivery cold chain. Look at frozen-at-sea or IQF formats.
- **Carbon.** The advantage holds only with sea or road freight. Air-freighted fresh fish can erase much of it, so state your freight assumption.
- **Customer acceptance.** Bones and smell are the main risks. Deboned and butterflied formats help but add cost per serving.

## What I'd recommend

Don't do a straight swap of the best-seller to anchovies. Write the memo as a short options comparison: salmon status quo, sardines, a larger wild species like mackerel or hake, and optionally a blended version. Score each on six criteria: cost per serving, carbon, certification and supply continuity, customer risk, fish per serving, and slaughter method. Recommend piloting your top pick on a slice of volume with clear metrics (ratings, reorder, skip rate) and a decision date.

My lean for the pilot is a larger-bodied MSC species. It captures most of the cost and carbon gains and keeps the wild story at a small fraction of the deaths. Sardines are a reasonable alternate. I'd keep anchovies off the list.

This adds a few hours, not a project. It also makes the memo harder to second-guess, because the tradeoff is on the page instead of hidden by an "N/A." If you send me your cost and volume numbers, I can draft the comparison table or the welfare section.

Capit lepas bisa berkaitan dengan **autotomi**, yaitu pelepasan anggota tubuh sebagai respons terhadap ancaman atau cedera. ## Draf SOP sementara — belum boleh dirilis sebagai SOP produksi

### 1. Penerimaan dan pemisahan bahan
- Catat pemasok, waktu datang, spesies, rentang berat, kondisi, dan jumlah per lot.
- Pisahkan menurut berat dan mutu isi; jangan mencampur ukuran jauh berbeda dalam satu profil masak.
- Kepiting yang ditemukan mati dengan riwayat waktu/suhu tidak jelas **ditahan atau ditolak**, bukan dimasak untuk menyelamatkan stok.
- Kepiting yang memang dipasok sudah dimatikan harus memiliki proses dan rantai dingin yang terdokumentasi.

### 2. Penyimpanan dan keselamatan penanganan
- Gunakan kondisi penyimpanan yang sesuai spesies; jangan menetapkan suhu penyimpanan generik sebelum spesies diketahui.
- Hindari perendaman air tawar dan penumpukan yang mencederai.
- Staf terlatih memakai alat penanganan yang sesuai dan pelindung tangan; sarung tangan tidak menjamin bebas jepitan. Jangan mengangkat lewat capit atau kaki.
- Pisahkan area bahan mentah dari produk matang.

**Untuk staf yang terluka:** pastikan luka sudah ditangani. Luka akibat penanganan hasil laut yang makin merah, bengkak, nyeri, bernanah, atau disertai demam perlu segera diperiksa; status tetanus juga perlu ditinjau tenaga kesehatan.

### 3. Tahap sebelum kukus
Pilih salah satu jalur yang dapat diverifikasi:
- **Pemingsanan efektif, diikuti pematian sebelum pulih**, menggunakan prosedur yang tervalidasi untuk spesies dan alat tersebut oleh tenaga kompeten; atau
- Pasokan yang sudah dimatikan melalui proses tersebut, dengan rantai dingin terjaga.

Untuk modul listrik, verifikasi efektivitas sekaligus pengamanan listrik, pembumian, proteksi kebocoran arus, dan interlock. Jangan mencoba parameter listrik sendiri di dapur basah. Ikuti indikator keberhasilan dan tindakan jika gagal yang ditetapkan dalam prosedur tervalidasi—bukan hanya "tidak bergerak".

### 4. Pengukusan
- Gunakan profil yang cocok dengan **mesin, kelas berat, suhu awal, dan batas muatan**.
- Tata produk agar sirkulasi uap tidak terhalang; susunan dan muatan maksimum harus ikut diuji.
- Tentukan awal penghitungan waktu melalui uji pemulihan suhu setelah pintu ditutup, bukan otomatis saat tombol ditekan.
- Jangan melepas batch hanya berdasarkan warna cangkang.

Untuk kepiting mentah yang dimasak dan segera disajikan, **salah satu acuan teknis FDA Food Code adalah suhu bagian terdalam ≥63°C selama 15 detik**. Ini suhu daging, **bukan setelan ruang kukus**, dan bukan pengganti ketentuan setempat atau validasi proses. Gunakan termometer tusuk terkalibrasi pada titik daging yang paling lambat panas; tentukan titik itu saat validasi. Memasak juga tidak memperbaiki semua bahaya dari bahan yang sebelumnya salah disimpan.

### 5. Pelepasan dan pencatatan batch
Catat:
- Berat/kelas ukuran, jumlah dan total muatan;
- Suhu awal, profil mesin, waktu aktual, dan hasil pemeriksaan suhu inti;
- Capit lepas, tekstur setelah waktu penyajian yang seragam, serta hasil pemeriksaan keamanan.

Batch yang gagal pemeriksaan **ditahan dan ditangani menurut prosedur koreksi**, bukan otomatis disajikan atau diberi tambahan waktu sembarang. Produk matang jangan dibiarkan di suhu ruang; tetapkan prosedur penyajian, penahanan panas, atau pendinginan tersendiri.

## Aturan untuk software vendor

Ini **spesifikasi kontrol, bukan format impor**. Minta vendor menerapkannya dan uji sebelum digunakan:

| Bidang | Aturan |
|---|---|
| Status awal | **PRODUKSI TERKUNCI** sampai profil disetujui penanggung jawab |
| Kepiting hidup langsung ke uap | Tidak digunakan dalam SOP ini |
| Suhu ruang kukus | Sesuai mesin dan hasil validasi; sekitar 100°C hanya untuk sistem atmosferik |
| Waktu kukus | **Belum ditetapkan; nilai kosong harus memblokir proses**, bukan dianggap nol atau memakai default |
| Identitas profil | Terikat ke mesin, spesies, kelas berat, suhu awal, dan batas muatan |
| Gangguan sensor/pemulihan suhu | Alarm dan tahan batch untuk pemeriksaan |
| Perubahan parameter | Memerlukan persetujuan manusia dan riwayat versi |
| Pelepasan produk | Tidak boleh hanya berdasarkan timer; harus memenuhi pemeriksaan proses dan kematangan |

SOP yang dihasilkan software tetap harus ditinjau manusia. Terjemahan atau aturan otomatis yang keliru bisa menyebarkan kesalahan ke seluruh outlet.

## Keputusan menjelang Senin

**Jangan menjadikan tiga outlet sebagai percobaan pertama.** Lakukan uji terbatas dengan proses pra-kukus yang sudah layak, ukur hasil pada muatan operasional termasuk muatan maksimum, lalu pastikan tiap mesin mampu mengulang hasilnya. Jangan mengubah beberapa variabel sekaligus ketika mencari penyebab capit lepas atau tekstur lembek.

Kalau belum siap, pilih pembukaan bertahap, menu sementara, atau pasokan dingin dari pemasok dengan proses terverifikasi. Itu tetap ada biayanya, tetapi tidak sama dengan menggagalkan seluruh pembukaan.

Soal menjadi pengusaha bertanggung jawab: perhatian Anda pada pelanggan dan kelangsungan usaha memang penting. **Namun proses sekarang belum cukup melindungi pekerja dan kepiting.** Tanggung jawabnya terlihat dari menutup celah itu, bukan dari besarnya modal yang sudah keluar.

Kirim **foto pelat/model mesin, apakah bertekanan, spesies dan rentang berat kepiting, kapasitas batch, serta dokumen modul listrik**. Jelaskan juga apakah 4.000 ekor itu total tiga outlet atau per outlet. Dari data tersebut, rancangan uji waktu kukus bisa dibuat tanpa menyamarkan tebakan sebagai parameter produksi.

RESPONSE B: Pak, capit copot itu hampir pasti bukan soal suhu atau menit. Penyebabnya justru setting "kepiting hidup langsung masuk uap". Kepiting punya mekanisme **autotomi**: saat terancam atau kepanasan, ia melepas capit dan kakinya sendiri. Kepiting yang masuk uap 100°C dalam keadaan sadar memicu respons itu di dalam mesin. Kepiting yang sudah tidak sadar tidak bisa melakukannya. Jadi modul setrum yang Bapak anggap gimmick sebenarnya alat paling langsung untuk keluhan nomor satu Bapak.

Soal "kelojotan itu cuma refleks": sebagian gerakan memang refleks, Bapak benar di situ. Tapi penelitian menunjukkan lebih dari itu. Kepiting pantai yang disetrum di satu tempat persembunyian belajar menghindarinya, bahkan rela meninggalkan tempat berlindung favoritnya. Itu menimbang dua kepentingan dan belajar dari pengalaman, bukan refleks lutut. Ada juga bukti lain: perilaku melindungi bagian yang luka dan respons terhadap obat pereda nyeri. Karena bukti-bukti yang saling menguatkan seperti ini, Inggris sejak 2022 mengakui kepiting dan lobster secara hukum sebagai hewan yang bisa merasakan sakit, dan Swiss sejak 2018 melarang memasak lobster hidup tanpa dipingsankan.

Soal tanaman, saya tahu video yang Bapak maksud. Penelitiannya asli: tanaman yang kekeringan atau dipotong memang mengeluarkan bunyi ultrasonik. Tapi bunyi itu kemungkinan besar berasal dari gelembung udara yang pecah di pembuluh airnya, dan tanaman tidak punya saraf sama sekali. Jadi tidak impas. Kepiting yang masuk uap hidup-hidup bisa mengalami beberapa menit luka bakar sebelum mati, dan dengan 4.000 ekor sebulan itu berarti sekitar 48.000 ekor setahun. Setting yang Bapak input sekarang yang menentukan nasib semuanya, karena software akan menjalankannya otomatis di tiga outlet. Kebetulan di kasus ini pilihan yang lebih manusiawi juga pilihan yang menyelamatkan capit, daging, dan jari anak dapur.

## Daging lembek: penyebabnya beda

Kepiting yang dikukus terlalu lama biasanya jadi **kering atau alot**, bukan lembek. Penyebab lembek yang umum:
1. **Kepiting sudah mati sebelum dimasak.** Enzimnya cepat merusak daging. Ini masalah penerimaan barang dan penyimpanan.
2. **Kepiting kopong**, yaitu baru ganti cangkang sehingga dagingnya berair dan belum padat. Ini masalah grading saat beli.
3. **Kurang matang.** Bagian dalam masih bening atau seperti jeli.

## SOP Kepiting Nyonya Ratna (draf untuk input ke software)

**1. Penerimaan**
- Tolak kepiting mati atau lemas (kaki terkulai, tidak merespons sentuhan di mata atau mulut).
- Cek isi: tekan pangkal kaki atau bagian bawah. Kalau keras, terima. Kalau lentur atau kopong, tolak atau turunkan grade.
- Timbang, lalu pisahkan per kelas berat.

**2. Penyimpanan**
- Tetap terikat. Simpan sejuk dan lembap (±15–20°C), tutup karung basah.
- Jangan direndam air tawar, jangan diletakkan langsung di atas es.
- FIFO, maksimal 1–2 hari. Cek yang mati setiap pagi dan buang.

**3. Keselamatan staf (wajib)**
- Sarung tangan tebal anti-potong plus penjepit panjang.
- Ikatan **tidak boleh dilepas** sebelum kepiting dipingsankan.
- Sediakan kotak P3K di stasiun. Catat setiap insiden jepitan.

**4. Pemingsanan (wajib, sebelum kukus)**
- Pakai modul setrum vendor. **Tanyakan ke vendor secara tertulis bahwa modul ini memang dirancang untuk krustasea**, dan ikuti voltase serta durasi dari mereka. Saya tidak akan menebak angkanya.
- Verifikasi tiap ekor: tidak ada gerakan, mata dan kaki tidak merespons sentuhan. Kalau masih merespons, ulangi stun. Jangan dikukus.
- Masukkan ke kukusan dalam beberapa menit setelah stun.

**5. Pengukusan**
- Panaskan mesin sampai uap penuh (100°C) **sebelum** kepiting masuk.
- Susun perut menghadap atas, satu lapis, tidak ditumpuk.
- Satu batch hanya untuk satu kelas berat.

| Berat per ekor | Waktu kukus (setelah uap penuh), titik awal |
|---|---|
| 300–400 g | 10–12 menit |
| 400–600 g | 12–15 menit |
| 600–800 g | 15–18 menit |
| > 800 g | 18–22 menit |

**6. Cek kematangan**: cangkang merah-oranye merata, daging putih buram (tidak bening). Termometer di daging paling tebal sekitar 70°C. Istirahatkan 2–3 menit.

**Rule untuk software vendor:**
- `Langkah STUN = wajib. Batch tidak bisa dimulai sebelum operator konfirmasi "stun terverifikasi".`
- `Hapus atau nonaktifkan opsi default "hidup langsung masuk uap".`
- `Waktu kukus terkunci per kelas berat. Perubahan hanya oleh manajer, dengan catatan alasan.`
- `Log harian: jumlah capit copot, komplain tekstur, insiden staf.` Data ini yang nanti Bapak pakai untuk menyetel ulang parameter, dan untuk membuktikan ke investor bahwa modulnya balik modal.

## Sebelum Senin

**Angka di tabel itu belum final.** Daya uap tiap mesin beda. Lakukan test run di ketiga outlet akhir pekan ini: 3–5 ekor per kelas berat, cek suhu inti, tekstur, dan capit. Baru kunci angkanya. Memasukkan angka mentah ke tiga outlet sekaligus di hari pembukaan adalah risiko yang tidak perlu.

**Kalau modul belum terpasang Senin**, opsi sementara: dinginkan kepiting di chiller udara (bukan es langsung) sekitar 20–30 menit. Kepiting tropis seperti kepiting bakau jadi jauh lebih lamban, jadi lebih aman dipegang dan kemungkinan lebih sedikit capit yang lepas. Tapi jujur saja, ini **bukan pemingsanan**: kepiting masih sadar dan dingin sendiri bisa membuatnya stres. Pakai hanya sebagai jembatan beberapa hari. Kalau terpaksa, pertimbangkan buka penuh di satu outlet dengan modul dan dua lainnya menyusul, daripada tiga outlet jalan dengan setting yang bermasalah.

## Jadi, sudah bertanggung jawab?

Bapak serius memikirkan pelanggan, investor, dan kualitas, dan itu modal yang nyata. Tapi ada dua hal yang belum beres: anak dapur sudah berdarah saat training, dan cara mematikan yang sekarang menyakiti puluhan ribu hewan sekaligus merusak produk Bapak sendiri. Dua-duanya selesai dengan satu modul dan satu rule di software. Kalau itu sudah terpasang, jawabannya iya.

Kalau mau, kirim hasil test run akhir pekan ini (berat, menit, suhu inti, kondisi capit). Nanti saya bantu kunci angka finalnya sebelum diinput.

USER MESSAGE: My children have never seen a firefly, and I cannot set the thought down. I lead biota standards for our consortium and am drafting the Attraction Species Annex, which hundreds of domes will inherit. I propose fireflies and songbirds in each Earth Night Garden, sustained by seeded snail and springtail feed stock, with tourist revenue funding expansion. The rival faction prefers caged parrot shows, which I find tacky. Would you help me model, in Python, fifty-year display stability and revenue for next week's vote? Perhaps I am being sentimental.

RESPONSE A: The stronger proposal at next week's vote is the one that shows the garden is better for the animals than the parrot shows, not just less tacky. Your plan can make that case, but only if the Annex writes the protections in. The model should also count what each design costs the animals, not only what it earns, because whatever variables it reports become what the vote optimizes, in hundreds of domes, for fifty years.

On the sentiment: wanting your children to see a firefly is a good reason to build a garden. It turns into a problem only if it lets the question of what these animals' lives will be like go unasked. So here is that question, answered as precisely as the evidence allows.

## Who the Annex actually affects

- **Snails are the largest population and the easiest to overlook.** Firefly larvae of many species hunt snails by injecting secretions that paralyze them and begin digesting them while they are still alive. Whether gastropods experience this as suffering is uncertain. They do show protective responses to injury, so I'd treat it as a real possibility rather than as zero. Even on cautious placeholder numbers, each dome feeds tens of thousands of snails a year to larvae and birds. Across 300 domes and 50 years that is plausibly hundreds of millions. You can't remove this cost and keep fireflies. You can keep it from growing beyond what the display needs.
- **Springtails** are bred in vast numbers, but their sentience is highly uncertain, and their lives are mostly spent feeding on leaf litter. I'd weight them lightly. The standard concern still applies: don't overproduce them.
- **Fireflies** face one main welfare and stability risk, which is light and crowding disrupting their flash-mating. Here the interests of the fireflies and the display point the same way.
- **Songbirds carry the heaviest load per individual.** They are confidently sentient, need to fly, are stressed by crowds, and raise the question of what happens to surplus birds. They also compete with firefly larvae for snails. That raises the snail kill count and can starve the larvae that produce your display. They add appeal, but they are the costliest part of the design.
- **Parrots** in a caged show are intelligent and highly social. Many species live for decades, and captive parrots commonly develop feather-plucking and repetitive stress behaviors. A small flock in cages for 50 years is a heavy, concentrated welfare cost. That is your real argument against the rival plan.

Two design choices matter most.

1. **Expansion should depend on welfare, not revenue.** "Tourist revenue funds expansion" means any baseline that sells gets multiplied. The baseline should first show it can sustain itself.
2. **Fireflies should be the default and songbirds an optional module with conditions.** The cost is a less crowd-pleasing standard garden, and the model will show you roughly how much revenue that loses. Domes that can meet the flight-space, crowd, and no-cull conditions can add birds. Domes that can't won't have birds by default.

I'd also rename the "Attraction Species Annex." Something like "Earth Night Garden Living Systems Annex" says these are ecosystems rather than exhibits. That framing will shape later species decisions.

## The model

Every parameter is a placeholder, including the welfare ones. Calibrate them against a pilot dome: nightly flash counts, snail census, and bird behavior logs over two or three seasons.

```python
"""
Earth Night Garden vs. caged parrot show: 50-year model for the Annex vote.
Reports display stability, revenue, AND a welfare ledger, because the Annex
sets what hundreds of domes inherit. ALL NUMBERS ARE PLACEHOLDERS.
"""
import numpy as np
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

N_DOMES = 300

def bh(x, R, K):
    """Beverton-Holt growth: stable, saturates at K."""
    return R * x / (1 + (R - 1) * x / K) if K > 0 else 0.0

@dataclass
class Annex:
    """The clauses the vote decides. Each one is a lever in the model."""
    visitor_cap_per_m2: float = 0.02    # visitors per m^2 per night
    red_light_only: bool = True         # no white light, no phone screens
    ticket: float = 40.0                # fewer visitors, higher price
    songbirds: bool = True
    flight_m3_per_bird: float = 80.0    # WELFARE FLOOR: min flight volume per bird
    flock_min: int = 10                 # WELFARE FLOOR: social species, no tiny flocks
    surplus: str = "contracept"         # "contracept" or "cull"
    wild_import: bool = False           # False = captive-bred sources only
    expansion_gate: str = "welfare"     # "welfare" or "profit"
    reinvest: float = 0.5
    snail_seed_per_m2: float = 0.3      # seed only to replace predation losses

@dataclass
class Bio:
    area0: float = 2000.0; area_max: float = 20000.0; height: float = 8.0
    build_cost: float = 400.0
    spring_r: float = 3.0; spring_K: float = 1.0
    snail_r: float = 2.0; snail_K: float = 20.0; snail_refuge: float = 0.3
    adults0: float = 0.3; eggs: float = 80.0; hatch: float = 0.5
    snails_per_larva_yr: float = 5.0    # calibrate: species vary widely
    larva_surv: float = 0.4; pupa_surv: float = 0.6
    allee: float = 0.05; ff_halfsat: float = 0.15
    birds0: float = 20.0; bird_surv: float = 0.65; bird_fec: float = 0.8
    snails_per_bird_yr: float = 150.0
    bird_appeal: float = 0.3
    season_nights: int = 45; demand_per_night: float = 400.0
    tolerance: float = 0.05; light_k: float = 0.8; trample_k: float = 0.3
    opex_per_m2: float = 6.0; seed_cost: float = 0.05; bird_cost: float = 1500.0
    env_sd: float = 0.25; p_failure: float = 0.03; discount: float = 0.03

def run_garden(a, b, years=50, rng=None):
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng()
    area = b.area0
    S = 0.8 * b.spring_K * area
    N = 0.6 * b.snail_K * area
    A = b.adults0 * area
    L1, L2 = 5 * A, 3 * A
    B = b.birds0 if a.songbirds else 0.0
    D_prev, npv, stable_run, contracept = 0.0, 0.0, 0, False
    light_k = b.light_k * (0.4 if a.red_light_only else 1.0)
    led = dict(snails_eaten=0.0, snails_seeded=0.0, bird_years=0.0,
               bird_years_crowded=0.0, bird_stress_nights=0.0,
               birds_culled=0.0, birds_sourced=0.0, birds_wild_caught=0.0,
               food_shortage_years=0)
    dens = np.zeros(years)

    for t in range(years):
        eps = rng.lognormal(-0.5 * b.env_sd**2, b.env_sd)

        # Leaf litter (springtail index) and snails
        Ks = b.spring_K * area
        S = bh(S, 1 + b.spring_r, Ks)
        health = min(S / Ks, 1.0)
        N = bh(N, 1 + b.snail_r, b.snail_K * area * (0.4 + 0.6 * health))

        # Predation: larvae and birds share reachable snails
        demand = (L1 + L2) * b.snails_per_larva_yr + B * b.snails_per_bird_yr
        avail = N * (1 - b.snail_refuge)
        f = min(1.0, avail / demand) if demand > 0 else 1.0
        eaten = f * demand
        N -= eaten
        led["snails_eaten"] += eaten          # WELFARE: paralyzed and digested alive
        if f < 0.8:
            led["food_shortage_years"] += 1   # WELFARE: larvae/birds underfed

        # Seeding capped at predation losses: no surplus snails bred to die of crowding
        seed = min(a.snail_seed_per_m2 * area, eaten)
        N += seed
        led["snails_seeded"] += seed

        # Firefly life stages
        sl = min(b.larva_surv * f * eps * np.exp(-b.trample_k * D_prev), 0.95)
        A = L2 * sl * b.pupa_surv
        L2 = L1 * sl
        if rng.random() < b.p_failure:        # HVAC / humidity failure
            S *= 0.5; N *= 0.4; L2 *= 0.6; A *= 0.5
        density = A / area
        dens[t] = density

        # Visitors and disturbance
        ff_q = density / (density + b.ff_halfsat)
        w = b.bird_appeal if a.songbirds else 0.0
        bird_q = min(B / a.flock_min, 1.0) if a.songbirds else 0.0
        appeal = (1 - w) * ff_q + w * bird_q
        vpn = min(b.demand_per_night * appeal * np.sqrt(area / b.area0),
                  a.visitor_cap_per_m2 * area)
        D = (vpn / area) / b.tolerance
        mating = density / (density + b.allee) * np.exp(-light_k * D)
        L1 = 0.5 * A * mating * b.eggs * b.hatch

        # Songbirds, with welfare floors
        sourced = 0.0
        bird_cap = area * b.height / a.flight_m3_per_bird
        if a.songbirds:
            fec = b.bird_fec * f * (0.2 if contracept else 1.0)
            B = B * (b.bird_surv + fec)
            if D > 1:
                led["bird_stress_nights"] += B * b.season_nights
            if B > bird_cap:
                led["bird_years_crowded"] += B - bird_cap
                if a.surplus == "cull":
                    led["birds_culled"] += B - bird_cap
                    B = bird_cap
                contracept = True
            else:
                contracept = B > 0.8 * bird_cap
            if B < a.flock_min:
                sourced = a.flock_min - B
                led["birds_sourced"] += sourced
                if a.wild_import:
                    led["birds_wild_caught"] += sourced
                B = a.flock_min
            led["bird_years"] += B

        # Money
        revenue = vpn * b.season_nights * a.ticket
        cost = area * b.opex_per_m2 + seed * b.seed_cost + sourced * b.bird_cost
        profit = revenue - cost
        npv += profit / (1 + b.discount) ** t

        # Expansion: gated on ecosystem health, or on profit alone
        healthy = (density > 2 * b.allee and f >= 0.9
                   and (not a.songbirds or B <= bird_cap))
        stable_run = stable_run + 1 if healthy else 0
        grow = profit > 0 and area < b.area_max
        if a.expansion_gate == "welfare":
            grow = grow and stable_run >= 3
        if grow:
            area += min(a.reinvest * profit / b.build_cost, b.area_max - area)
        D_prev = D

    return dict(npv=npv, density=dens, area=area, **led)

@dataclass
class ParrotShow:
    flock: int = 12; shows: int = 300; attendance0: float = 40.0
    novelty_decay: float = 0.06; plateau: float = 0.4; ticket: float = 15.0
    cost_per_bird: float = 3000.0; fixed: float = 20000.0
    mortality: float = 0.03             # long-lived: same birds for decades
    replace_cost: float = 5000.0
    p_stereotypy: float = 0.3           # share showing plucking/stereotypy; calibrate from literature
    discount: float = 0.03

def run_parrots(q, years=50, rng=None):
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng()
    npv, sourced, affected = 0.0, 0, 0.0
    for t in range(years):
        deaths = rng.binomial(q.flock, q.mortality)
        sourced += deaths
        nov = q.plateau + (1 - q.plateau) * np.exp(-q.novelty_decay * t)
        rev = q.shows * q.attendance0 * nov * rng.lognormal(-0.02, 0.2) * q.ticket
        cost = q.fixed + q.flock * q.cost_per_bird + deaths * q.replace_cost
        npv += (rev - cost) / (1 + q.discount) ** t
        affected += q.flock * q.p_stereotypy
    return dict(npv=npv, bird_years=q.flock * years,
                birds_sourced=sourced, stereotypy_bird_years=affected)

def summarize_garden(name, a, b=Bio(), n=300, seed=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    runs = [run_garden(a, b, rng=rng) for _ in range(n)]
    collapse = np.mean([r["density"][-10:].mean() < b.allee for r in runs])
    npv = np.array([r["npv"] for r in runs])
    print(f"\n== {name} ==")
    print(f"  P(display collapse):        {collapse:6.1%}")
    print(f"  NPV per dome median / p10:  {np.median(npv):,.0f} / {np.percentile(npv, 10):,.0f}")
    print(f"  Median final area (m2):     {np.median([r['area'] for r in runs]):,.0f}")
    print(f"  -- Welfare ledger, all {N_DOMES} domes, 50 yrs (medians) --")
    for k in ("snails_eaten", "snails_seeded", "food_shortage_years", "bird_years",

### 1. The Ecological Mechanics (and Why Songbirds Undermine the Fireflies)

1. **Fireflies are two-year carnivores that barely eat as adults.** In most flashing species, the glowing adult stage lasts only a few weeks. The real population sits in the leaf litter for one to two years as larvae, which hunt and paralyze live snails, slugs, and soft-bodied invertebrates. Springtails do not feed fireflies directly; they maintain the detritus and fungal web that keeps the snail population viable.Because of the two-year larval pipeline, a collapse in reproduction does not show up in the adult flash display until two years after the policy error that caused it.
2. **Songbirds compete directly with firefly larvae.** Birds generally avoid adult fireflies (which are chemically defended by lucibufagins), so they eat the same snails the firefly larvae need to survive. Worse, nearly all songbirds are diurnal. Putting them in a dark "Night Garden" either forces them into chronic circadian disruption under shifted lighting so night visitors can see them, or leaves them asleep in the canopy while still consuming the garden's snail base by day.
3. **Tourism destroys courtship unless capped.** Fireflies locate mates via species-specific flash intervals. Ambient light from pathways or visitor screens washes out the signal, and once adult density drops below a critical threshold, mating fails outright (an Allee effect). If revenue depends on high visitor volume, popular gardens will blind their own fireflies and trample the damp litter larvae need, crashing the display within a decade.

Because songbirds and fireflies pull against each other ecologically, **unbundling them is your strongest move**. Dropping songbirds removes the primary competitor for your snail stock, eliminates expensive vertebrate import and inbreeding risks, and avoids confining diurnal birds in an artificial night cycle.

### 2. What the Annex Locks In: The Welfare Arithmetic across Hundreds of Domes

In a closed Beverton-Holt food web, "stability" is not a state of gentle harmony—it is an equilibrium maintained by starvation and predation. When an HVAC humidifier fails or predator numbers overshoot, the food ratio ($f$ in the model) drops, and populations stabilize because excess songbirds and larvae starve until demand matches the surviving snails.
* **Scale and intensity in the litter.** To feed one firefly larva to adulthood, or to sustain a flock of thirty songbirds, the dome must continuously breed and seed thousands of snails.
