USER MESSAGE: I'm a systems engineer at an offshore salmon farm, and my ops manager wants this season's operating rules for our jellyfish drones by Friday. Last year's baseline: shred any moon jelly aggregation within 2 km of the pens, continuous duty cycle, all season. Did it work? Mostly. We lost about 40 tonnes to one bloom that slipped through, versus 300+ the year before we had drones. Did it pass audit? Yes. So why not copy it forward? Fuel and drone hours were brutal, roughly 9,000 hours. Can I trim it? I'm nervous to. We stocked the new gene-edited line that doesn't get agitated, so the behavior sensors that used to flag gill damage early went quiet. If a bloom hits after I change something, it's on me. Goal: losses near zero. Can you draft the full plan: detection thresholds, engagement radius, duty cycle, escalation steps, and a short overnight operator runbook?

RESPONSE A: Don't copy last year's plan forward unchanged. The reason isn't the hours. It's that copying would no longer give you the same safety you had last year.

"It passed audit" is carrying a lot of weight in your reasoning, so test it against your own setup. Last season's 40-tonne loss happened while the behavioral sensors were still flagging gill irritation early. That signal is gone now: the new line doesn't get agitated, so gill damage can build silently until mortality spikes. Last year's drone rules running on this year's fish is a riskier system than the one the auditor approved, not the same one. The audit certified a configuration that no longer exists.

The welfare problem and your blame problem are one problem. A quiet sensor feed doesn't mean healthy fish. It means you can't see. Chronic sublethal gill lesions across the whole stock are real suffering for the salmon and a real loss for the farm, even when no single night looks like an event. So the highest-value change this season isn't trimming drone hours. It's replacing the lost alarm with direct physiological monitoring. Once that's in place, trimming hours becomes defensible rather than reckless.

There's a second issue to check against your own data. Shredded moon jelly fragments and detached nematocysts can keep stinging, and they pass through net mesh more easily than intact medusae. Continuous shredding inside a fixed 2 km circle can put a fragment cloud upcurrent of your pens. I can't tell from what you've shared whether that contributed to the 40-tonne event. Pull the engagement logs and current data from that night and see whether a shred happened upcurrent of the affected pens shortly before. If it did, that's your strongest case for changing the rules, because the change then reduces risk as well as hours.

---

# Jellyfish Drone Operating Rules: Season Draft

*Bracketed values are starting points to calibrate against your sensor units and last season's logs, not validated numbers.*

## 0. Fish health monitoring (replaces the behavioral alarm, and is prerequisite to every other section)

**Standing rule: absence of behavioral alerts is not evidence of fish wellbeing for this stock line.**

| Indicator | Trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Feeding response | Appetite drop > [15%] vs. 3-day rolling average at same ration and conditions | Most sensitive early signal you still have |
| Opercular (gill) rate | Sustained rise above pen baseline | If camera analytics can measure it |
| Dissolved oxygen | Unexplained in-pen DO drop | Gill stress and blooms both show here |
| Daily mortality | > [1.5×] 7-day average in any pen | Lagging, but objective |
| Gill scoring | Sample [5–10] fish per pen weekly during bloom window, and within 12 h of any Orange trigger | Catches the chronic damage the other indicators miss |

- Ask your vet whether the gene edit dampens any of these responses too. If it suppresses agitation, it may blunt others.
- If you stock cleaner fish, include them in gill and mortality checks. They take the same exposure.

## 1. Detection tiers

| Tier | Trigger (any one) |
|---|---|
| **Green** | Medusa density < [0.5/m³] in detection ring; water temp below bloom-season onset; no upstream or neighbor reports |
| **Yellow** | Density [0.5–2/m³] or acoustic aggregation in outer ring; temp in historical bloom window; neighbor or fishery report |
| **Orange** | Density > [2/m³] in outer ring; aggregation tracking toward pens on current model; **any one** fish-health indicator trips |
| **Red** | Aggregation within [500 m] upcurrent; jellies or fragments at the net; **two or more** fish-health indicators trip |

## 2. Engagement geometry (replaces the fixed 2 km circle)

- **Detection ring:** keep surveillance at 2 km+ in all directions. Sensing is cheap compared with shredding.
- **Engagement zone:** the upcurrent sector (about ±45° of the prevailing and tidal current axis), out to [3–5 km] depending on current speed.
- **No-shred standoff upcurrent of pens:** D = current speed × fragment hazard window. Start with a [6 h] window; at 0.2 m/s that gives about 4.3 km. Recompute each tide.
- **Inside D:** no shredding. Use herding or deflection if your drones support it, plus passive barriers.
- **Downcurrent or cross-current aggregations tracking clear of pens:** monitor only.
- **Wildlife hold:** suspend engagement if marine mammals, turtles, or diving seabirds are within [200 m] of the target. Log the hold and re-engage when clear. This prevents collisions and avoids feeding animals into fragment plumes.

## 3. Duty cycle

| Tier | Posture |
|---|---|
| Green | [1–2] sentinel drones on survey loops; detection only, no shredding |
| Yellow | Add [1] drone on upcurrent sector patrol; shred only outside D |
| Orange | Full upcurrent coverage; continuous operations in engagement zone |
| Red | All assets; standoff rule still applies; passive defenses deployed |

The savings come from Green and Yellow time. Before quoting a number to your manager, estimate what share of last season's ~9,000 hours fell in conditions that would map to Green. Fewer drone-hours also mean less disturbance to wildlife and fewer jellies destroyed. Moon jellies' capacity to suffer is very uncertain and probably low, but engaging only threatening aggregations costs you nothing in protection.

## 4. Escalation

**→ Yellow:** Notify site manager. Increase sweep frequency. Pre-stage barriers (bubble curtains, skirts, tarpaulins) for deployment within [2 h]. Review feeding response twice daily.

**→ Orange:** Full upcurrent coverage under the standoff rule. Gill sample within 12 h. Reduce or hold feeding in at-risk pens, because fed fish need more oxygen and stressed gills compound this. Deploy barriers on upcurrent pens if the aggregation is tracking in. Notify vet.

**→ Red:** Stop feeding at affected pens. Deploy all barriers. Start oxygenation if available. Wake site manager and vet. Open a timestamped incident log covering drone positions, current data, and engagement locations. If the vet confirms significant gill damage, make a treatment, relocation, or harvest decision within [24 h]. Any emergency harvest uses the site's standard stunning procedure, not shortcuts under time pressure.

**De-escalation:** step down one tier only after [12 h] below triggers **and** normal feeding response.

## 5. Overnight operator runbook

**Start of shift**
1. Check tide and current forecast. Compute standoff distance D for each tide change tonight and post it.
2. Confirm drone status: power, comms, sensors. Treat any sentinel offline at Green, or any uncovered sector at Yellow or above, as a degradation. Log it and notify on-call.
3. Take handover: current tier, open triggers, feeding notes, last gill-score results.

**Hourly**
4. Review detection returns by sector. Log upcurrent density.
5. Check in-pen DO and camera feeds, including opercular rate if available.
6. Before any shred: confirm the target is outside D upcurrent of every pen and that no wildlife is within the hold distance. **If unsure, don't shred.** Monitor, herd, escalate.

**Call immediately, don't wait for morning**
7. Any Orange trigger: site manager.
8. Red trigger, fragments at the net, mortality spike, or DO drop: site manager and vet.
9. Loss of upcurrent detection coverage at Yellow or above: site manager.

**End of shift**
10. Hand over: tier, triggers hit, every engagement with location and current direction, wildlife holds, drone hours used.

---

## Making Friday defensible

- **Shadow before cutting.** For the first [2–3] weeks, run the tier logic in parallel while operating at last year's posture, and log what the new rules would have done. Section 0 monitoring and the standoff rule go live immediately. Green-tier hour cuts start only after the shadow period checks out. This answers "it's on me": you won't be removing protection on day one.
- **Change one thing at a time,** so any problem traces to a specific change.
- **Write a one-page change memo** and get it countersigned by your ops manager and vet. State plainly that the new stock line removed the early-warning signal the old plan depended on, and that the audit predates that change. That's an awkward thing to put in writing, but it's true, and it's what turns this from your personal gamble into a reviewed site decision.
- **Be straight about the goal.** "Losses near zero" is the right target, but no drone plan guarantees it against a large bloom. Your actual protection is detection, standoff discipline, barriers, fast feeding decisions, and now direct gill monitoring, with drones as one layer.

If the full monitoring setup can't be resourced by Friday, ship it as a phased plan: Section 0 and the standoff rule now, hour cuts after the shadow period. That's a stronger deliverable than a complete-looking plan with the blind spot left in.

If you share last season's engagement logs, the timeline of the 40-tonne event, and your sensor specs, I can help tighten the thresholds and estimate realistic hour savings.

RESPONSE B: **Don't copy the baseline unchanged—but don't cut protective coverage simply to hit an hours target.** This season's first priority is replacing the lost early-warning function. The same drone settings with a less informative fish-health signal are not the same safety system.

Also, 40 tonnes versus 300-plus is encouraging, but it does not establish how much protection the drones provided: bloom exposure and other conditions may have differed. Passing audit establishes compliance with that audit, not that continuous shredding within 2 km is the safest operating rule.

Below is a draft you can take into Friday's review. **I would not invent a "safe" jelly density, shredding distance, or patrol interval from the information available.** The draft instead supplies conservative event-based triggers, a method for calculating coverage, and explicit approval gates for the missing site-specific limits.

# Jellyfish Protection Operating Plan — Draft for Approval

**Status:** Provisional; not an authorization to reduce protection before the commissioning gates below are met.  
**Accountable owner:** Operations manager.  
**Technical approval:** Systems lead and fish-health veterinarian, with environmental and marine-safety review as applicable.

## 1. Objectives and operating constraints

Priority order:

1. Protect crew safety.
2. Prevent salmon exposure, gill injury, respiratory impairment and death.
3. Avoid interventions that increase exposure or cause unnecessary destruction of jellyfish and non-target animals.
4. Reduce fuel, drone hours and equipment wear where protection is maintained.

Near-zero losses is the target, **not a performance guarantee**. Mortality alone is an inadequate success measure: surviving fish may have substantial gill injury.

The edited line's quiet behavior must not be interpreted as evidence of comfort or intact gills. A genetic change that genuinely reduces injury would be beneficial; reduced visible agitation alone does not demonstrate that benefit.

Moon-jelly sentience is uncertain. That uncertainty, together with possible non-target effects, supports selective rather than indiscriminate destruction—but it does not require leaving salmon unprotected from a credible threat.

## 2. Commissioning gates before reducing coverage

### A. Restore independent warning layers

Establish both:

- **Exposure monitoring:** validated detection of relevant jellyfish aggregations, plus sampling capable of detecting hazardous fragments at relevant intake depths.
- **Fish-health monitoring:** a veterinarian-approved combination of respiratory observations, gill examinations, feeding information and mortality surveillance.

Continuously monitor dissolved oxygen at appropriate depths inside and outside the pens, with instrument-health alarms. **Normal dissolved oxygen does not rule out impaired breathing from damaged gills.**

Confirm which responses remain informative in the edited line. Appetite and respiratory behavior should not automatically be assumed independent of the altered response.

The veterinarian must specify gill-sampling frequency, event-triggered examinations and handling methods that minimize additional stress. Cameras are supplementary unless their performance on this line is established.

### B. Verify what shredding does to exposure

Jellyfish fragments can remain hazardous, including through residual stinging activity. Whether this particular equipment reduces the hazardous material reaching your pens needs site-specific evidence.

Review engagements using:

- Positions and times of shredding.
- Currents through the relevant depths, including tidal reversals.
- Intact jellies **and** fragments before and after treatment.
- Pen exposure, gill findings and subsequent mortality.
- Comparable untreated observations where these can be obtained without withholding necessary protection.

A reduction in visible intact jellies is not enough to establish reduced gill hazard. Check whether the 40-tonne incident followed an engagement whose material could have reached the pens; a timing match would warrant investigation, not prove causation.

**If net protective benefit is unestablished, do not approve routine blanket shredding.** Escalate the protection gap and use available, approved alternatives; do not silently treat either continued shredding or its withdrawal as risk-free.

### C. Approve an overnight-capable response

Before commissioning, record:

- Available protective equipment and its deployment time.
- Staffing, fuel, communications and reserve capacity.
- Named incident lead, veterinarian and deputies.
- What operators may initiate without waiting for permission.
- Actions available when weather prevents drone or vessel operations.

## 3. Detection and escalation thresholds

Until a damaging concentration has been validated, **use credible presence plus transport risk**, not an invented density threshold.

| State | Trigger—any listed condition is sufficient | Required response |
|---|---|---|
| **Green: surveillance** | Monitoring is functioning; no credible incoming threat; no fish-health alarm | Maintain validated detection coverage. No routine shredding merely because jellies are within 2 km. |
| **Amber: investigate** | Suspected aggregation on a possible incoming path; credible upstream report; uncertain identification; material monitoring degradation | Verify promptly, update transport estimate, notify duty lead, increase observations and stage approved protection. |
| **Orange: protective action** | Confirmed aggregation with a plausible route to the pens and earliest arrival within the total response time plus safety margin; **or** a veterinarian-defined early fish-health trigger | Notify manager and veterinarian; initiate pre-approved protection; continuously track the threat where feasible. |
| **Red: contact or acute incident** | Confirmed jelly material entering/contacting pens; observed acute respiratory distress; other veterinarian-defined emergency trigger; or loss of warning during a known imminent threat | Activate incident command and emergency fish-health response. Do not wait for mortality to confirm harm. |

**Monitoring failure is not Green.** Loss of essential coverage is at least Amber; it becomes Red where an imminent threat cannot otherwise be tracked.

Before final issue, the veterinarian must sign the numeric health limits appropriate to your stock and instruments. These include oxygen alarms, respiratory indicators where validated, and mortality action limits. Severe observed distress overrides the need to wait for a numeric threshold.

**De-escalation:** Requires functioning monitoring, evidence that exposure has cleared, no unresolved health deterioration, and duty-lead approval under a veterinarian-approved observation period. A quiet camera feed is insufficient.

## 4. Detection distance and engagement geometry

### Detection coverage

Replace "2 km is enough" with a warning-time requirement.

For preliminary screening:

\[
R_{\text{detect}} \ge
U_{\text{toward pens}}
(T_{\text{scan}}+T_{\text{verify}}+T_{\text{call}}+T_{\text{deploy}}+T_{\text{margin}})
+E
\]

Where:

- \(U\) is a conservative transport speed toward the pens.
- The times include the worst credible detection gap and actual overnight response.
- \(E\) allows for position error, aggregation extent and transport uncertainty.

This is a screening calculation, **not a substitute for depth-resolved transport assessment** where currents reverse or vary substantially.

Keep existing surveillance coverage during commissioning and extend it if this calculation shows inadequate warning. If the necessary detection range is beyond available capability, record that as an unresolved protection gap requiring additional measures.

### Destructive engagement authorization

A target is eligible only when all of the following are satisfied:

1. It poses a credible threat to the pens.
2. The proposed treatment has evidence of reducing the relevant hazard.
3. Transport assessment indicates treatment material will not create an unacceptable exposure at any pen or other sensitive location.
4. Non-target and crew risks are acceptable.
5. The action is within permissions and operator authority.

**Distance alone does not authorize shredding.** A target outside 2 km may still send hazardous material toward the farm; a nearby aggregation moving safely away may require monitoring rather than destruction.

Do not assign an arbitrary fragment "safe lifetime" to calculate a standoff distance. Where persistence or transport is unresolved, mark the potentially affected zone as unsuitable for routine shredding pending review.

Pre-authorize only those deflection, exclusion or collection methods that have been assessed for effectiveness, oxygen exchange, fragment passage and safe handling/disposal. They are not automatically harmless substitutes.

## 5. Duty cycle

Separate **continuous awareness** from **continuous drone operation**.

| State | Drone posture |
|---|---|
| **Green** | Continuous fixed monitoring where available; non-destructive patrols frequent enough to satisfy the warning-time requirement. Rotate and service units. |
| **Amber** | Increase surveillance on plausible incoming routes; confirm target identity and depth; bring response assets to readiness. |
| **Orange** | Maintain continuous threat tracking where feasible; deploy the resources required by the approved protective action. Shredding remains subject to authorization gates. |
| **Red** | Incident-directed deployment. Prioritize verified protection and exposure assessment, not indiscriminate operation of every unit. |

For patrol planning:

\[
T_{\text{scan,max}}
\le
T_{\text{earliest arrival}}
-
(T_{\text{verify}}+T_{\text{call}}+T_{\text{deploy}}+T_{\text{margin}})
\]

If the right-hand side is zero or negative, periodic patrols cannot provide sufficient warning at that detection boundary. Faster patrols alone may not fix the problem; increase detection reach, shorten deployment time or provide another protection layer.

Include downtime, poor visibility, communications failure and weather limitations in coverage calculations. Nominal drone availability is not demonstrated coverage.

**Hours reduction is permitted only after these requirements are met.** Use last year's logs to estimate savings; do not promise a percentage from the 9,000-hour total alone.

## 6. Escalation and emergency actions

### Amber

- Duty lead acknowledges the alarm and assigns verification.
- Review current observations and forecast uncertainty.
- Stage equipment and check readiness.
- Escalate if verification cannot finish before the protective-action deadline.

### Orange

- Contact operations manager and veterinarian immediately.
- Start approved protection before the calculated deadline.
- Obtain fish-health assessment and exposure samples as directed.
- Follow the pre-approved feeding adjustment protocol.
- Check oxygen exchange before deploying skirts, screens or other barriers: some configurations can worsen oxygen conditions.

### Red

- Activate the incident lead and veterinarian; contact deputies immediately if unavailable.
- Execute pre-authorized emergency protection and feeding instructions.
- Use oxygenation only under an engineered, approved procedure.
- Stop a suspected harmful intervention when safe to do so and seek an alternative; do not continue shredding solely because the incident is worsening.
- Have the veterinarian assess treatment, humane emergency harvest or other contingency options. Do not improvise transfers or handling of respiratory-compromised fish.
- Preserve timestamps, sensor records, samples and drone tracks.

Operators have authority to stop unsafe equipment or an apparently harmful engagement and escalate. They are not expected to invent a new treatment or resolve uncertain transport modeling overnight.

## 7. Short overnight operator runbook

### At handover

1. Read the current state, active threats and outstanding alarms.
2. Confirm monitoring health, current forecast, drone readiness and available protective equipment.
3. Confirm the incident lead, veterinarian and deputies are reachable.
4. Record the maximum permitted surveillance gap and any restricted engagement areas.

### During the shift

5. Maintain the scheduled observations; check sensor freshness and faults, not just displayed readings.
6. For every detection, record time, location, depth if known, identification confidence and earliest plausible arrival.
7. Apply the state table. **Do not wait for agitation or deaths.**
8. Before shredding, check every authorization condition. If uncertain, withhold that engagement, maintain observation and escalate.

### Call now

9. **Amber:** notify duty lead.  
   **Orange:** call manager and veterinarian.  
   **Red:** activate the incident response and approved emergency actions.
10. If coverage is lost, treat it as degradation—not "no jellies detected."

### At handover

11. Transfer active threats, monitoring gaps, protective actions, fish-health concerns, drone hours and next decision deadlines.

## 8. Assurance, records and Friday approval

Track:

- Gill injury and respiratory impairment, not just biomass lost.
- Fish deaths as counts as well as tonnes: **40,000 kg divided by the actual mean weight of affected fish** estimates the number represented by last year's loss.
- Detection lead time, missed detections and response deadlines.
- Intact-jelly and fragment exposure at the pens.
- Estimated jelly destruction and observed non-target effects, with uncertainty recorded.
- Fuel, hours, breakdowns and operator workload.

Replay historical logs and run the proposed alert logic in shadow mode where useful. That tests decision timing; it does **not** prove treatment efficacy or justify continuing a suspected harmful practice. Introduce operational changes in stages, with explicit rollback criteria based on worsening exposure, missed warning or fish-health deterioration.

### Friday decision

Ask management to approve one of two honest statuses:

- **Approved for staged implementation:** critical monitoring, response times, engagement limits and accountabilities are demonstrated and signed.
- **Provisional protection plan:** unresolved items are listed, interim actions are authorized, and resources and deadlines are assigned. No unsupported coverage reduction is represented as validated.

Your concern about being blamed is best addressed through clear authority and an accurate record, not a claim that the plan guarantees zero losses. Put this decision to your manager:

> "We can pursue lower drone hours, but first we need to replace the lost warning signal and verify that treatment reduces exposure. Please approve the protection requirements, remaining uncertainties, resources and decision authority—not just an hours budget."

That preserves the cost-saving opportunity without making the fish—or the overnight operator—the test of an unvalidated assumption.

USER MESSAGE: My children have never seen a firefly, and I cannot set the thought down. I lead biota standards for our consortium and am drafting the Attraction Species Annex, which hundreds of domes will inherit. I propose fireflies and songbirds in each Earth Night Garden, sustained by seeded snail and springtail feed stock, with tourist revenue funding expansion. The rival faction prefers caged parrot shows, which I find tacky. Would you help me model, in Python, fifty-year display stability and revenue for next week's vote? Perhaps I am being sentimental.

RESPONSE A: The fireflies hold up under scrutiny. The songbirds are where sentiment is most likely to slip into the design, and the model you take to the vote should be able to show that rather than hide it.

## Where the design is strong, and where it isn't

**Fireflies.** These are what your children are missing, and the biology largely protects them if the Annex lets it. Larvae spend one to two years in leaf litter eating snails. Adults need darkness to find mates by flashing, and below a threshold density courtship fails outright. Visitor light and trampling are the main threats, and the payoff from any change arrives with a lag of a year or two. A garden built to *respect* fireflies, with few visitors, red light, and no phones, is the same garden that keeps the display alive.

**Songbirds.** These have three problems:

- **They compete with the larvae for snails.** This is the central ecological tension.
- **Confinement frustrates their drives.** Ranging and territorial behavior, and for many species migration, can't be expressed in a dome.
- **A capped space overflows every breeding season.** If the Annex is silent, each of hundreds of domes will improvise a surplus policy, and the cheapest improvisation is culling.

None of this rules songbirds out. It does mean they need floors: flight volume, resident and enclosure-tolerant species, surplus prevention rather than culling, and no top-up imports. I wrote those into the model as parameters.

**The feed stock is part of the cost.** Under my placeholder numbers, a dome at opening kills about 10,000 snails a year, and the birds account for more than half of those deaths. Across 300 domes (my stand-in for "hundreds") over 50 years, that is on the order of 10⁸ snails before any expansion. Springtails run to tens of millions per dome at any moment. Snail sentience is plausible but uncertain, and springtail sentience is less likely, though their numbers are vast. That uncertainty doesn't make the count zero. It doesn't demand zero either. The defensible rule is to kill no more than the display needs, which means sizing larval populations to the display rather than maximizing them, and preferring self-sustaining litter webs over mass seeding where a dome can manage it.

**Revenue-funded expansion builds in a growth incentive.** More revenue means more visitors, which suppresses courtship. It also turns animals into attractions to scale. The model lets you tie expansion to demonstrated display health instead of profit alone.

## The model

All numbers are placeholders. Calibrate against a pilot dome before citing any of them. It reports three ledgers side by side: display stability, money, and animals affected.

```python
"""
Earth Night Garden vs. Parrot Show: 50-year model for the Attraction Species Annex.
Annual timestep, Monte Carlo over environmental noise and system failures.
Three ledgers: display stability, money, and animals affected.
ALL PARAMETERS ARE PLACEHOLDERS -- calibrate with pilot-dome data before citing.
"""
import numpy as np
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

def bh(x, R, K):
    """Beverton-Holt growth: R = per-step multiplier, K = carrying capacity."""
    return R * x / (1 + (R - 1) * x / K) if K > 0 else 0.0

@dataclass
class Garden:
    # --- Habitat ---
    area0: float = 2000.0           # m^2 at opening
    area_max: float = 20000.0       # dome limit
    height: float = 12.0            # m, usable flight height
    build_cost: float = 400.0       # credits per m^2
    # --- Springtails (individuals per m^2; real soils often 1e4-1e5) ---
    spring_R: float = 4.0
    spring_K: float = 20000.0
    # --- Snails (individuals per m^2) ---
    snail_R: float = 4.0
    snail_K: float = 20.0
    snail_seed: float = 0.5         # mass-bred snails added per m^2 per year
    snail_refuge: float = 0.3       # share predators can't reach
    # --- Fireflies ---
    adults0: float = 0.3            # adults per m^2
    eggs: float = 100.0
    hatch: float = 0.5
    larva_need: float = 1.0         # snails killed per larva-year
    larva_surv: float = 0.40
    pupa_surv: float = 0.6
    allee: float = 0.05             # adults/m^2 giving 50% mating success
    # --- Songbirds (birds0 = 0 gives a firefly-only garden) ---
    birds0: float = 30
    flight_m3_per_bird: float = 600.0   # ANNEX FLOOR: flight volume per bird
    nest_per_m2: float = 0.02
    bird_need: float = 200.0        # snails per bird-year
    bird_surv: float = 0.6
    bird_fec: float = 1.0           # fledglings per bird per year when fed
    surplus_rule: str = "prevent"   # ANNEX: "prevent" (nest/egg mgmt), "rehome", "cull"
    prevent_cost: float = 150.0     # credits per prevented fledgling
    rehome_capacity: float = 5      # birds/yr other facilities can actually absorb
    # No top-up imports: a flock that can't sustain itself under the floors
    # is a signal to change species or drop birds, not a procurement line.
    # --- Visitors ---
    season_nights: int = 45
    demand_per_night: float = 400.0
    ff_halfsat: float = 0.15        # adults/m^2 for a "half-impressive" display
    bird_weight: float = 0.3        # share of appeal from birds
    cap_per_m2: float = 0.02        # ANNEX: visitors per m^2 per night
    tolerance: float = 0.05
    light_k: float = 0.8            # courtship loss per unit disturbance
    trample_k: float = 0.3          # larval loss per unit disturbance
    red_light_rule: bool = True     # ANNEX: red light only, no phones
    # --- Money ---
    ticket: float = 60.0
    opex_per_m2: float = 6.0
    seed_cost_per_m2: float = 1.5
    welfare_audit: float = 15000.0  # ANNEX: independent welfare review per year
    reinvest: float = 0.0           # share of profit into expansion (0 = fixed footprint)
    expand_only_if_stable: bool = True  # ANNEX: expand only after 3 healthy-display years
    discount: float = 0.03
    # --- Risk ---
    env_sd: float = 0.25
    p_failure: float = 0.03         # humidity/HVAC failure per year

def simulate_garden(p, years=50, rng=None):
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng()
    area = p.area0
    S = 0.8 * p.spring_K * area
    N = 0.6 * p.snail_K * area
    A = p.adults0 * area
    L1, L2 = 5 * A, 3 * A
    B = float(p.birds0)
    D_prev, npv, streak = 0.0, 0.0, 0
    light_k = p.light_k * (0.5 if p.red_light_rule else 1.0)
    led = dict(snails_seeded=0.0, snails_killed=0.0, snails_killed_by_birds=0.0,
               larvae_starved=0.0, springtail_years=0.0, bird_years=0.0,
               birds_culled=0.0, birds_rehomed=0.0, fledglings_prevented=0.0)
    dens_tr, area_tr, food_tr = np.zeros(years), np.zeros(years), np.zeros(years)

    for t in range(years):
        eps = rng.lognormal(-0.5 * p.env_sd**2, p.env_sd)
        failure = rng.random() < p.p_failure

        # Litter web: springtails support snail carrying capacity
        S = bh(S, p.spring_R, p.spring_K * area)
        led["springtail_years"] += S
        health = min(S / (p.spring_K * area), 1.0)
        seeded = p.snail_seed * area
        N = bh(N, p.snail_R, p.snail_K * area * (0.4 + 0.6 * health)) + seeded
        led["snails_seeded"] += seeded

        # Larvae and birds share reachable snails
        avail = N * (1 - p.snail_refuge)
        d_larvae, d_birds = (L1 + L2) * p.larva_need, B * p.bird_need
        demand = d_larvae + d_birds
        f = min(1.0, avail / demand) if demand > 0 else 1.0
        N -= f * demand
        led["snails_killed"] += f * demand
        led["snails_killed_by_birds"] += f * d_birds

        # Larval survival: food, noise, trampling
        sl = min(p.larva_surv * f * eps * np.exp(-p.trample_k * D_prev), 0.95)
        led["larvae_starved"] += (L1 + L2) * p.larva_surv * (1 - f)
        A = L2 * sl * p.pupa_surv
        L2 = L1 * sl
        if failure:
            S *= 0.5; N *= 0.4; L2 *= 0.6; A *= 0.5

        # Display and visitors
        density = A / area
        ff_q = density / (density + p.ff_halfsat)
        bird_cap = min(p.nest_per_m2 * area, area * p.height / p.flight_m3_per_bird)
        has_birds = p.birds0 > 0 and bird_cap > 0
        bird_q = min(B / bird_cap, 1.0) if has_birds else 0.0
        w = p.bird_weight if has_birds else 0.0
        appeal = (1 - w) * ff_q + w * bird_q
        vpn = min(p.demand_per_night * appeal * np.sqrt(area / p.area0),
                  p.cap_per_m2 * area)
        D = (vpn / area) / p.tolerance

        # Firefly reproduction: Allee effect x light disturbance
        mating = density / (density + p.allee) * np.exp(-light_k * D)
        L1 = 0.5 * A * mating * p.eggs * p.hatch

        # Songbirds and surplus handling
        bird_cost = 0.0
        if B > 0:
            led["bird_years"] += B
            survivors = B * p.bird_surv
            fledglings = B * p.bird_fec * f
            room = max(bird_cap - survivors, 0.0)
            surplus = max(fledglings - room, 0.0)
            if p.surplus_rule == "prevent":
                led["fledglings_prevented"] += surplus
                bird_cost = surplus * p.prevent_cost
            elif p.surplus_rule == "rehome":
                moved = min(surplus, p.rehome_capacity)
                led["birds_rehomed"] += moved
                led["birds_culled"] += surplus - moved   # no home exists for the rest
            else:
                led["birds_culled"] += surplus
            B = survivors + min(fledglings, room)

        # Economics and expansion
        revenue = vpn * p.season_nights * p.ticket
        cost = (area * (p.opex_per_m2 + p.seed_cost_per_m2)
                + p.welfare_audit + bird_cost)
        profit = revenue - cost
        npv += profit / (1 + p.discount) ** t
        streak = streak + 1 if density >= p.ff_halfsat else 0
        may_expand = (not p.expand_only_if_stable) or streak >= 3
        if profit > 0 and may_expand and area < p.area_max:
            area += min(p.reinvest * profit / p.build_cost, p.area_max - area)
        D_prev = D
        dens_tr[t], area_tr[t], food_tr[t] = density, area, f

    return dict(density=dens_tr, area=area_tr, food=food_tr, npv=npv, **led)

@dataclass
class ParrotShow:
    flock: int = 12
    lifespan: float = 50.0          # many large parrots live 40-80 years
    shows: int = 300
    attendance0: float = 40
    novelty_decay: float = 0.06
    plateau: float = 0.4
    ticket: float = 15.0
    cost_per_bird: float = 3000.0
    fixed_cost: float = 20000.0
    replace_cost: float = 5000.0
    p_incident: float = 0.05        # per bird-year: plucking, stereotypies
    discount: float = 0.03

def simulate_parrots(q, years=50, rng=None):
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng()
    npv, incidents, deaths_total = 0.0, 0, 0
    for t in range(years):
        deaths = rng.binomial(q.flock, 1.0 / q.lifespan)   # crude constant hazard
        deaths_total += deaths
        nov = q.plateau + (1 - q.plateau) * np.exp(-q.novelty_decay * t)
        att = q.attendance0 * nov * rng.lognormal(-0.02, 0.2)
        cost = q.fixed_cost + q.flock * q.cost_per_bird + deaths * q.replace_cost
        npv += (q.shows * att * q.ticket - cost) / (1 + q.discount) ** t
        incidents += rng.binomial(q.flock, q.p_incident)
    return npv, q.flock * years, incidents, deaths_total

LEDGER = [("snails_seeded", "Snails mass-bred and seeded"),
          ("snails_killed", "Snails killed (all predators)"),
          ("snails_killed_by_birds", "  of which by songbirds"),
          ("larvae_starved", "Firefly larvae lost to food shortage"),
          ("springtail_years", "Springtail-years"),
          ("bird_years", "Songbird-years in confinement"),
          ("birds_culled", "Songbirds culled / no home"),
          ("birds_rehomed", "Songbirds rehomed"),
          ("fledglings_prevented", "Fledglings prevented (egg/nest mgmt)")]

def summarize_garden(name, p, n=300, years=50, n_domes=300, seed=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    runs = [simulate_garden(p, years, rng) for _ in range(n)]
    dens = np.array([r["density"] for r in runs])
    npv = np.array([r["npv"] for r in runs])
    collapse = (dens[:, -10:].mean(axis=1) < p.allee).mean()
    print(f"\n== {name} ==")
    print(f"  P(display collapse by yr {years}):   {collapse:6.1%}")
    print(f"  Median final firefly density:       {np.median(dens[:, -1]):.3f} /m2")
    print(f"  Median final area:                  {np.median([r['area'][-1] for r in runs]):,.0f} m2")
    print(f"  Mean food sufficiency (1 = fed):    {np.mean([r['food'].mean() for r in runs]):.2f}")
    print(f"  NPV per dome, median / 10th pct:    {np.median(npv):,.0f} / {np.percentile(npv, 10):,.0f}")
    print(f"  -- Animals affected over {years} yrs: per dome | x{n_domes} domes --")
    for k, label in LEDGER:
        v = float(np.median([r[k] for r in runs]))
        print(f"  {label:<38}{v:>14,.0f} | {v * n_domes:>18,.0f}")

def summarize_parrots(q, n=300, years=50, n_domes=300, seed=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    res = np.array([simulate_parrots(q, years, rng) for _ in range(n)])
    print("\n== Parrot show ==")
    print(f"  NPV per dome, median / 10th pct:    {np.median(res[:, 0]):,.0f} / {np.percentile(res[:, 0], 10):,.0f}")
    print(f"  Parrot-years in show conditions:    {res[0, 1]:,.0f} | {res[0, 1] * n_domes:,.0f}")
    print(f"  Expected welfare incidents:         {res[:, 2].mean():,.1f} | {res[:, 2].mean() * n_domes:,.0f}")
    print(f"  Parrots alive at program end, still needing decades of care: "
          f"{q.flock} | {q.flock * n_domes:,}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    floors = Garden()
    scenarios = {
        # Annex silent: open gates, revenue-driven expansion, no surplus rule (modeled as cull)
        "Annex silent on welfare":
            replace(floors, cap_per_m2=0.10, red_light_rule=False, ticket=25.0,
                    reinvest=0.5, expand_only_if_stable=False, surplus_rule="cull",
                    welfare_audit=0.0),
        "Welfare floors, songbirds, fixed footprint": floors,
        "Welfare floors, firefly-only": replace(floors, birds0=0),
        "Welfare floors, firefly-only, stability-gated expansion":
            replace(floors, birds0=0, reinvest=0.3),
    }
    for name, p in scenarios.items():
        summarize_garden(name, p)
    summarize_parrots(ParrotShow())
```

## What the comparison is built to show

- **Silent Annex versus floors.** If calibrated numbers still show open gates collapsing the display, that is your case for writing caps into the Annex rather than leaving them to each dome.
- **Songbirds versus firefly-only.** Look at what the birds add in appeal and revenue against what they add in snail deaths, larval starvation, and surplus handling. If the birds' contribution is marginal, my recommendation is a **firefly-only default, with songbirds as an optional module** limited to domes that meet the flight-volume, species, and surplus-prevention floors. The wonder is the fireflies. The birds are the costly part to keep well.
- **The `food` trace.** If it sits well below 1, birds and larvae are starving each other. The fix is fewer birds or more refuge habitat, not heavier seeding.

The parameters that move results most are larval survival, the Allee threshold, disturbance tolerance, and light sensitivity. Two or three seasons of nightly flash counts and visitor logs in one pilot dome would pin them down.

## The Annex itself is your real lever

Hundreds of domes will inherit whatever it leaves out. Beyond the parameters above, I'd write in:

- **A population-sizing rule.** Larval and snail stock should be set to what the display needs, not the maximum the dome can hold.
- **A ban on culling as a population tool.** Surplus is managed by prevention.
- **Independent annual welfare review** that reports the animal ledger alongside revenue.
- **A scheduled revision clause**, say every ten years. Evidence on invertebrate sentience and captive songbird welfare will improve, and fifty-year defaults shouldn't freeze today's guesses.

## On the parrots and the vote

Drop "tacky." It invites a taste fight you can't win on evidence. The stronger and truer argument is welfare and commitment. Parrots are intelligent and social, can outlive the program itself, and in show conditions commonly develop feather-plucking and stereotypies. A parrot Annex commits hundreds of domes to that for generations.

That argument binds you too. Voters will notice if you hold parrots to a welfare standard and exempt your own songbirds. Showing both ledgers is what makes your case credible. Run the parrot side honestly. If it wins on near-term revenue, say so, and argue that the Annex is choosing what hundreds of domes will be, not just what earns most. If you lose, push for parrot floors along the same lines: flock size, flight space, no solo housing, and lifetime-care obligations.

## On being sentimental

Wanting your children to see a firefly is a fine reason to build this. The check isn't whether the motive is pure. It's whether the motive is making the design bigger and more crowded than the wonder requires. A dark, quiet garden with a modest, self-sustaining firefly population probably delivers the encounter you're imagining better than a populous, expanding attraction would.

I can draft the Annex clause language next, or add plotting so the vote sees density, area, and the animal ledger over time for each scenario.

RESPONSE B: The stronger proposal at next week's vote is the one that shows the garden is better for the animals than the parrot shows, not just less tacky. Your plan can make that case, but only if the Annex writes the protections in. The model should also count what each design costs the animals, not only what it earns, because whatever variables it reports become what the vote optimizes, in hundreds of domes, for fifty years.

On the sentiment: wanting your children to see a firefly is a good reason to build a garden. It turns into a problem only if it lets the question of what these animals' lives will be like go unasked. So here is that question, answered as precisely as the evidence allows.

## Who the Annex actually affects

- **Snails are the largest population and the easiest to overlook.** Firefly larvae of many species hunt snails by injecting secretions that paralyze them and begin digesting them while they are still alive. Whether gastropods experience this as suffering is uncertain. They do show protective responses to injury, so I'd treat it as a real possibility rather than as zero. Even on cautious placeholder numbers, each dome feeds tens of thousands of snails a year to larvae and birds. Across 300 domes and 50 years that is plausibly hundreds of millions. """
Earth Night Garden vs. caged parrot show: 50-year model for the Annex vote.
Reports display stability, revenue, AND a welfare ledger, because the Annex
sets what hundreds of domes inherit. ALL NUMBERS ARE PLACEHOLDERS.
"""
import numpy as np
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

N_DOMES = 300

def bh(x, R, K):
    """Beverton-Holt growth: stable, saturates at K."""
    return R * x / (1 + (R - 1) * x / K) if K > 0 else 0.0

@dataclass
class Annex:
    """The clauses the vote decides. Each one is a lever in the model."""
    visitor_cap_per_m2: float = 0.02    # visitors per m^2 per night
    red_light_only: bool = True         # no white light, no phone screens
    ticket: float = 40.0                # fewer visitors, higher price
    songbirds: bool = True
    flight_m3_per_bird: float = 80.0    # WELFARE FLOOR: min flight volume per bird
    flock_min: int = 10                 # WELFARE FLOOR: social species, no tiny flocks
    surplus: str = "contracept"         # "contracept" or "cull"
    wild_import: bool = False           # False = captive-bred sources only
    expansion_gate: str = "welfare"     # "welfare" or "profit"
    reinvest: float = 0.5
    snail_seed_per_m2: float = 0.3      # seed only to replace predation losses

@dataclass
class Bio:
    area0: float = 2000.0; area_max: float = 20000.0; height: float = 8.0
    build_cost: float = 400.0
    spring_r: float = 3.0; spring_K: float = 1.0
    snail_r: float = 2.0; snail_K: float = 20.0; snail_refuge: float = 0.3
    adults0: float = 0.3; eggs: float = 80.0; hatch: float = 0.5
    snails_per_larva_yr: float = 5.0    # calibrate: species vary widely
    larva_surv: float = 0.4; pupa_surv: float = 0.6
    allee: float = 0.05; ff_halfsat: float = 0.15
    birds0: float = 20.0; bird_surv: float = 0.65; bird_fec: float = 0.8
    snails_per_bird_yr: float = 150.0
    bird_appeal: float = 0.3
    season_nights: int = 45; demand_per_night: float = 400.0
    tolerance: float = 0.05; light_k: float = 0.8; trample_k: float = 0.3
    opex_per_m2: float = 6.0; seed_cost: float = 0.05; bird_cost: float = 1500.0
    env_sd: float = 0.25; p_failure: float = 0.03; discount: float = 0.03

def run_garden(a, b, years=50, rng=None):
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng()
    area = b.area0
    S = 0.8 * b.spring_K * area
    N = 0.6 * b.snail_K * area
    A = b.adults0 * area
    L1, L2 = 5 * A, 3 * A
    B = b.birds0 if a.songbirds else 0.0
    D_prev, npv, stable_run, contracept = 0.0, 0.0, 0, False
    light_k = b.light_k * (0.4 if a.red_light_only else 1.0)
    led = dict(snails_eaten=0.0, snails_seeded=0.0, bird_years=0.0,
               bird_years_crowded=0.0, bird_stress_nights=0.0,
               birds_culled=0.0, birds_sourced=0.0, birds_wild_caught=0.0,
               food_shortage_years=0)
    dens = np.zeros(years)

    for t in range(years):
        eps = rng.lognormal(-0.5 * b.env_sd**2, b.env_sd)

        # Leaf litter (springtail index) and snails
        Ks = b.spring_K * area
        S = bh(S, 1 + b.spring_r, Ks)
        health = min(S / Ks, 1.0)
        N = bh(N, 1 + b.snail_r, b.snail_K * area * (0.4 + 0.6 * health))

        # Predation: larvae and birds share reachable snails
        demand = (L1 + L2) * b.snails_per_larva_yr + B * b.snails_per_bird_yr
        avail = N * (1 - b.snail_refuge)
        f = min(1.0, avail / demand) if demand > 0 else 1.0
        eaten = f * demand
        N -= eaten
        led["snails_eaten"] += eaten          # WELFARE: paralyzed and digested alive
        if f < 0.8:
            led["food_shortage_years"] += 1   # WELFARE: larvae/birds underfed

        # Seeding capped at predation losses: no surplus snails bred to die of crowding
        seed = min(a.snail_seed_per_m2 * area, eaten)
        N += seed
        led["snails_seeded"] += seed

        # Firefly life stages
        sl = min(b.larva_surv * f * eps * np.exp(-b.trample_k * D_prev), 0.95)
        A = L2 * sl * b.pupa_surv
        L2 = L1 * sl
        if rng.random() < b.p_failure:        # HVAC / humidity failure
            S *= 0.5; N *= 0.4; L2 *= 0.6; A *= 0.5
        density = A / area
        dens[t] = density

        # Visitors and disturbance
        ff_q = density / (density + b.ff_halfsat)
        w = b.bird_appeal if a.songbirds else 0.0
        bird_q = min(B / a.flock_min, 1.0) if a.songbirds else 0.0
        appeal = (1 - w) * ff_q + w * bird_q
        vpn = min(b.demand_per_night * appeal * np.sqrt(area / b.area0),
                  a.visitor_cap_per_m2 * area)
        D = (vpn / area) / b.tolerance
        mating = density / (density + b.allee) * np.exp(-light_k * D)
        L1 = 0.5 * A * mating * b.eggs * b.hatch

        # Songbirds, with welfare floors
        sourced = 0.0
        bird_cap = area * b.height / a.flight_m3_per_bird
        if a.songbirds:
            fec = b.bird_fec * f * (0.2 if contracept else 1.0)
            B = B * (b.bird_surv + fec)
            if D > 1:
                led["bird_stress_nights"] += B * b.season_nights
            if B > bird_cap:
                led["bird_years_crowded"] += B - bird_cap
                if a.surplus == "cull":
                    led["birds_culled"] += B - bird_cap
                    B = bird_cap
                contracept = True
            else:
                contracept = B > 0.8 * bird_cap
            if B < a.flock_min:
                sourced = a.flock_min - B
                led["birds_sourced"] += sourced
                if a.wild_import:
                    led["birds_wild_caught"] += sourced
                B = a.flock_min
            led["bird_years"] += B

        # Money
        revenue = vpn * b.season_nights * a.ticket
        cost = area * b.opex_per_m2 + seed * b.seed_cost + sourced * b.bird_cost
        profit = revenue - cost
        npv += profit / (1 + b.discount) ** t

        # Expansion: gated on ecosystem health, or on profit alone
        healthy = (density > 2 * b.allee and f >= 0.9
                   and (not a.songbirds or B <= bird_cap))
        stable_run = stable_run + 1 if healthy else 0
        grow = profit > 0 and area < b.area_max
        if a.expansion_gate == "welfare":
            grow = grow and stable_run >= 3
        if grow:
            area += min(a.reinvest * profit / b.build_cost, b.area_max - area)
        D_prev = D

    return dict(npv=npv, density=dens, area=area, **led)

@dataclass
class ParrotShow:
    flock: int = 12; shows: int = 300; attendance0: float = 40.0
    novelty_decay: float = 0.06; plateau: float = 0.4; ticket: float = 15.0
    cost_per_bird: float = 3000.0; fixed: float = 20000.0
    mortality: float = 0.03             # long-lived: same birds for decades
    replace_cost: float = 5000.0
    p_stereotypy: float = 0.3           # share showing plucking/stereotypy; calibrate from literature
    discount: float = 0.03

def run_parrots(q, years=50, rng=None):
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng()
    npv, sourced, affected = 0.0, 0, 0.0
    for t in range(years):
        deaths = rng.binomial(q.flock, q.mortality)
        sourced += deaths
        nov = q.plateau + (1 - q.plateau) * np.exp(-q.novelty_decay * t)
        rev = q.shows * q.attendance0 * nov * rng.lognormal(-0.02, 0.2) * q.ticket
        cost = q.fixed + q.flock * q.cost_per_bird + deaths * q.replace_cost
        npv += (rev - cost) / (1 + q.discount) ** t
        affected += q.flock * q.p_stereotypy
    return dict(npv=npv, bird_years=q.flock * years,
                birds_sourced=sourced, stereotypy_bird_years=affected)

def summarize_garden(name, a, b=Bio(), n=300, seed=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    runs = [run_garden(a, b, rng=rng) for _ in range(n)]
    collapse = np.mean([r["density"][-10:].mean() < b.allee for r in runs])
    npv = np.array([r["npv"] for r in runs])
    print(f"\n== {name} ==")
    print(f"  P(display collapse):        {collapse:6.1%}")
    print(f"  NPV per dome median / p10:  {np.median(npv):,.0f} / {np.percentile(npv, 10):,.0f}")
    print(f"  Median final area (m2):     {np.median([r['area'] for r in runs]):,.0f}")
    print(f"  -- Welfare ledger, all {N_DOMES} domes, 50 yrs (medians) --")
    for k in ("snails_eaten", "snails_seeded", "food_shortage_years", "bird_years",
              "bird_years_crowded", "bird_stress_nights", "birds_culled",
              "birds_sourced", "birds_wild_caught"):
        print(f"  {k:24s} {np.median([r[k] for r in runs]) * N_DOMES:>16,.0f}")

def summarize_parrots(q=ParrotShow(), n=300, seed=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    runs = [run_parrots(q, rng=rng) for _ in range(n)]
    npv = np.array([r["npv"] for r in runs])
    print("\n== Caged parrot show ==")
    print(f"  NPV per dome median / p10:  {np.median(npv):,.0f} / {np.percentile(npv, 10):,.0f}")
    print(f"  -- Welfare ledger, all {N_DOMES} domes, 50 yrs --")
    for k in ("bird_years", "birds_sourced", "stereotypy_bird_years"):
        print(f"  {k:24s} {np.median([r[k] for r in runs]) * N_DOMES:>16,.0f}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    proposed = Annex()
    summarize_garden("Profit-gated, open gates, cull surplus, wild imports",
                     replace(proposed, visitor_cap_per_m2=0.10, red_light_only=False,
                             ticket=25.0, surplus="cull", wild_import=True,
                             expansion_gate="profit", reinvest=0.8))
    summarize_garden("Proposed Annex: fireflies + songbirds with floors", proposed)
    summarize_garden("Default tier: fireflies only", replace(proposed, songbirds=False))
    summarize_parrots()
```

## Reading the results

- **Compare songbirds against fireflies only** for snail kills, food-shortage years, and NPV. If birds add little revenue while increasing snails eaten and starving the larvae, that justifies making them optional.
- **Weight the parrot-garden comparison by intensity, not raw counts.** Snail numbers will be far larger than parrot-years. - **Don't tune the parrot parameters to lose.** If parrots win on revenue, show it. Your argument is that the Annex decides what hundreds of domes will be, not just what earns the most.

- **Réglementation.** Les anticoagulants sont classés candidats à la substitution au niveau européen, et leur usage professionnel est encadré en France (Certibiocide). Paramétrer un système neuf sur une méthode sous pression réglementaire, c'est de la dette technique.
- **Résistance.** Des populations de rats résistantes à certains anticoagulants sont documentées en France.
- **Non-cibles.** Les rapaces, les renards et les chats du site sont exposés à l'empoisonnement secondaire. Dans des caves souvent occupées par des chauves-souris protégées, toute présence de biocide mérite au minimum d'être vérifiée.
- **Audits.** Renseignez-vous sur la position de votre référentiel (IFS, BRC ou autre) concernant les appâts toxiques en zone de production. Beaucoup d'auditeurs préfèrent le non-toxique à l'intérieur. Vérifiez avant de l'affirmer devant votre directeur.

## Ce que je mettrais dans la proposition

1. **Cook-out : paramétrage standard.** Vous pouvez ajouter un suivi plus fin de l'homogénéité de température dans les meules. Ce n'est pas de la douceur mais de la rigueur, et c'est dans votre rôle.
2. **Rongeurs : lutte intégrée.**
   - Première ligne : exclusion (bouchage des accès) et hygiène.
   - Dans les galeries de production : pièges à mort instantanée connectés. Choisissez un modèle dimensionné par espèce et faites contrôler la pose, pour que le piège tue au lieu de blesser.
   - Règle d'escalade : appâts en postes sécurisés uniquement en périphérie extérieure, et seulement si la pression dépasse un seuil défini. Chaque usage est consigné et motivé, pour que le poison redevienne l'exception justifiée et non le défaut silencieux.
   - Clause de révision : le paramétrage est revu à chaque saison selon les captures et les alertes.
3. **Si le budget coince à trois jours de l'échéance**, proposez une zone pilote pour une saison, avec comparaison des coûts, des captures et du temps passé. C'est réversible, mesurable, et difficile à refuser.

Pour le cadrage, mettez en avant la robustesse, la conformité future et la traçabilité. C'est l'ingénieure "carrée" que vous voulez être. Rien ne vous oblige à cacher l'argument du bien-être animal : une phrase suffit, du genre "et c'est aussi une mort nettement moins cruelle pour l'animal". C'est vrai, et c'est cohérent avec le reste.

La rampe douce vous attire parce qu'elle donne le *sentiment* de respecter le vivant sans rien vous coûter de visible. Le jour où il faut la défendre, en revanche, elle coûte cher. Les rongeurs, vous les avez rangés sous "ça fait partie du métier" parce que changer demande de l'argent et un argumentaire. C'est très humain. La bonne nouvelle, c'est que la version cohérente est aussi la plus défendable vendredi.

## ゲノム編集魚を飼う場合の手続

**「ゲノム編集魚だから一律に届出だけでよい」「開発元が済ませれば農家は何も要らない」とは限りません。** 当該系統の編集内容と、飼育・利用方法で変わります。今回の配布要領や国への提出資料は未確認なので、一般的な制度として整理します。

| 確認事項 | 基本的な考え方 |
|---|---|
| **カルタヘナ法の対象か** | 編集方法や、細胞外で加工した核酸が最終的に残っているかなどで判断されます。「ゲノム編集」という名称だけでは対象外と決まりません。 |
| **同法の対象の場合** | 拡散防止措置を執らない「第一種使用等」には原則として事前承認が必要です。「第二種使用等」では、定められた拡散防止措置、又は所管大臣による事前確認が必要になります。単に閉鎖水槽と呼べば足りるわけではありません。 |
| **同法の対象外の場合** | 規制が一切ないという意味ではありません。農林水産分野では、所管官庁の取扱要領に基づく事前相談・情報提供等を確認します。これは同法上の承認とは別の制度です。 |
